sentences.zh: 【後唐紀三】 起旃蒙作噩十一月，盡柔兆閹茂三月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Records 3] From the eleventh month of Zhanmeng Zuoe through the third month of Rouzhao Yanmao—less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Tang Records 3] From the eleventh month of Zhanmeng Zuoe through the third month of Rouzhao Yanmao—less than a year in all.

sentences.zh: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝下同光三年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhuangzong Guangsheng Shenmin Xiaoxiao of Later Tang, Tongguang year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang, Tongguang year 3 (

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公元九二五年）

translations.literal: yiyou, AD 925)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, AD 925)

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙申，蜀主至成都，百官及後宮迎於七里亭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingshen, the Shu ruler arrived at Chengdu; the officials and the inner palace welcomed him at Qili Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day bingshen, the Shu ruler reached Chengdu, where officials and the inner palace met him at Qili Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 蜀主入妃嬪中作回鶻隊入宮。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler entered among the consorts and, forming a Uyghur-style procession, entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler walked in among his consorts in a Uyghur-style formation and entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，出見群臣於文明殿，泣下沾襟，君臣相視，竟無一言以救國患。

translations.literal: On dingyou he appeared before the ministers in the Hall of Civilization; tears soaked his robe, and ruler and ministers looked at one another yet found not a single word with which to remedy the state's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he received the ministers in the Hall of Civilization, weeping until his robe was wet; ruler and ministers gazed at one another, and in the end no one could utter a word that might save the realm.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，李紹琛至利州，修桔柏浮梁。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Li Shaochen reached Lizhou and repaired the floating bridge at Jubai.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Li Shaochen arrived at Lizhou and repaired the floating bridge at Jubai.

sentences.zh: 昭武節度使林思諤先棄城奔閬州，遣使請降。

translations.literal: The Zhaowu military commissioner Lin Si'e had already abandoned his city and fled to Langzhou, sending envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaowu military commissioner Lin Si'e had already abandoned his post and fled to Langzhou, where he sent envoys to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏王繼岌至劍州，蜀武信節度使兼中書令王宗壽以遂、合、渝、瀘、昌五州降。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Prince of Wei Li Jiji reached Jianzhou; the Shu Wuxin military commissioner and concurrent Grand Councillor Wang Zongshou surrendered the five prefectures of Sui, He, Yu, Lu, and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Prince of Wei Li Jiji reached Jianzhou; Wang Zongshou, Shu military commissioner of Wuxin and concurrent Grand Councillor, surrendered the five prefectures of Sui, He, Yu, Lu, and Chang.

sentences.zh: 王宗弼至成都，登大玄門，嚴兵自衛。

translations.literal: Wang Zongbi reached Chengdu, ascended the Great Mysterious Gate, and arrayed troops in strict guard for his own protection.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zongbi reached Chengdu, he mounted the Great Mysterious Gate and posted troops in tight array to guard himself.

sentences.zh: 蜀主及太后自往勞之，宗弼驕慢無復臣禮。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler and the empress dowager went in person to console him, but Zongbi was arrogant and insolent and no longer observed the rites due a subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler and the empress dowager went in person to comfort him, yet Zongbi was haughty and insolent and showed no further regard for the duties of a subject.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，劫遷蜀主及太后後宮諸王於西宮，收其璽綬，使親吏於義興門邀取內庫金帛，悉歸其家。

translations.literal: On yisi he forcibly moved the Shu ruler, the empress dowager, the inner palace, and the princes to the Western Palace, seized their seals and cords of office, and had trusted clerks at the Yixing Gate intercept gold and silks from the inner treasury, all of which he took to his own house.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he seized the Shu ruler, the empress dowager, the inner palace, and the princes and moved them to the Western Palace; he took their seals and cords of office and had trusted agents at the Yixing Gate seize gold and silks from the inner treasury and carry them all to his home.

sentences.zh: 其子承涓杖劍入宮，取蜀主寵姬數人以歸。

translations.literal: His son Cheng Juan entered the palace bearing a sword and took away several of the Shu ruler's favorite consorts.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng Juan entered the palace with sword in hand and carried off several of the Shu ruler's favorite consorts.

sentences.zh: 丙午，宗弼自稱權西川兵馬留後。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Zongbi styled himself acting military commissioner of the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Zongbi declared himself acting military commissioner of the western circuit.

sentences.zh: 李紹琛進至綿州，倉庫民居已為蜀兵所燔，又斷綿江浮梁，水深，無舟楫可渡，紹琛謂李嚴曰：「吾懸軍深入，利在速戰。

translations.literal: Li Shaochen advanced to Mianzhou; storehouses and dwellings had already been burned by Shu troops, and the floating bridge over the Mian River had been cut; the water was deep and there were no boats by which to cross. Shaochen said to Li Yan, "I have led an isolated army deep into enemy country—the advantage lies in swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaochen pressed on to Mianzhou, but Shu troops had already burned the storehouses and dwellings and destroyed the floating bridge over the Mian River; the water ran deep, and there were no boats to cross. Shaochen told Li Yan, "I have thrown an isolated army deep into enemy territory—our advantage lies in fighting fast.

sentences.zh: 乘蜀人破膽之時，但得百騎過鹿頭關，彼且迎降不暇；

translations.literal: While the Shu men are still shattered in spirit, if we can get even a hundred horsemen through Deer Head Pass, they will have no leisure but to come out and surrender;
translations.idiomatic: While the Shu are still demoralized, if we can get even a hundred horsemen through Deer Head Pass, they will be too busy rushing to surrender to resist;

sentences.zh: 若俟修繕橋樑，必留數日，或教王衍堅閉近關，折吾兵勢，倘延旬浹，則勝負未可知矣。」

translations.literal: if we wait to repair bridges and beams we must linger several days, or Wang Yan may be taught to shut the nearby passes firmly and break our army's momentum; should it drag on for ten days and more, then victory and defeat will be hard to know."
translations.idiomatic: if we wait to repair the bridges we will lose days, and someone may persuade Wang Yan to shut the nearby passes and blunt our momentum; if it drags on ten days or more, victory and defeat become uncertain."

sentences.zh: 乃與嚴乘馬浮渡江，從兵得濟者僅千人，溺死者亦千餘人，遂入鹿關頭；

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Yan rode their horses and swam across the river; of the followers only about a thousand got across, while more than a thousand drowned, and they then entered Deer Head Pass;
translations.idiomatic: He and Yan then rode their horses across the river; only about a thousand of their men got over, while more than a thousand drowned, and they entered Deer Head Pass.

sentences.zh: 丁未，進據漢州；

translations.literal: on dingwei they advanced and occupied Hanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei they advanced and seized Hanzhou;

sentences.zh: 居三日，後軍始至。

translations.literal: after three days the rear army at last arrived.
translations.idiomatic: three days passed before the rear army finally caught up.

sentences.zh: 王宗弼遣使以幣馬牛酒勞軍，且以蜀主書遺李嚴曰：「公來吾即降。」

translations.literal: Wang Zongbi sent envoys with gifts, horses, oxen, and wine to comfort the army, and also sent a letter from the Shu ruler to Li Yan saying, "When you come, I shall at once surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbi sent envoys with gifts, horses, cattle, and wine to reward the army, and forwarded a letter from the Shu ruler to Li Yan: "When you arrive, I will surrender at once."

sentences.zh: 或謂嚴：「公首建伐蜀之策，蜀人怨公深入骨髓，不可往。」

translations.literal: Someone told Yan, "You were the first to propose the plan to attack Shu; the Shu people hate you to the marrow— you must not go."
translations.idiomatic: Others warned Yan, "You were the first to urge the campaign against Shu; the Shu people hate you to the bone—you must not go."

sentences.zh: 嚴不從，欣然馳入成都，撫諭吏民，告以大軍繼至，蜀君臣後宮皆慟哭。

translations.literal: Yan would not heed this; gladly he galloped into Chengdu, reassured officials and people, and announced that the great army would follow; the Shu ruler, his ministers, and the inner palace all wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused to listen. He rode gladly into Chengdu, reassured officials and commoners, and announced that the main army was close behind; the Shu ruler, his ministers, and the inner palace all broke into lamentation.

sentences.zh: 蜀主引嚴見太后，以母妻為托。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler led Yan to see the empress dowager and entrusted his mother and wife to his care.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler brought Yan before the empress dowager and entrusted his mother and wife to him.

sentences.zh: 宗弼猶乘城為守備，嚴悉命撤去樓櫓。

translations.literal: Zongbi still manned the walls for defense; Yan ordered all watchtowers and parapets removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi still held the walls in a defensive posture, but Yan ordered every tower and parapet torn down.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏王繼岌至綿州，蜀主命翰林學士李昊草降表，又命中書待郎、同平章事王鍇草降書，遣兵部侍郎歐陽彬奉之以迎繼岌及郭崇韜。

translations.literal: On jiyou the Prince of Wei Li Jiji reached Mianzhou; the Shu ruler ordered Hanlin academician Li Hao to draft the surrender memorial, and also ordered Vice Grand Councillor and concurrent Chief Councillor Wang Kai to draft the surrender letter, sending Vice Minister of War Ouyang Bin to present them in welcome to Jiji and Guo Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Prince of Wei Li Jiji reached Mianzhou. The Shu ruler had Hanlin academician Li Hao draft the surrender memorial and Chief Councillor Wang Kai draft the surrender letter, then sent Vice Minister of War Ouyang Bin to present them and welcome Jiji and Guo Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 王宗弼稱蜀君臣久欲歸命，而內樞密使宋光嗣、景潤澄、宣徽使李周輅、歐陽晃熒惑蜀主；

translations.literal: Wang Zongbi declared that the Shu ruler and ministers had long wished to submit, but the inner privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and the palace commissioners Li Zhou'e and Ouyang Huang had deluded the Shu ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbi claimed that the Shu court had long wished to submit, but inner privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng and palace commissioners Li Zhou'e and Ouyang Huang had misled the Shu ruler;

sentences.zh: 皆斬之，函首送繼岌。

translations.literal: all were beheaded, their heads boxed and sent to Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: all were executed, their heads boxed and sent to Jiji.

sentences.zh: 又責文思殿大學士、禮部尚書、成都尹韓昭佞諛，梟於金馬坊門。

translations.literal: He also charged Wensi Hall academician, Minister of Rites, and Chengdu prefect Han Zhao with flattery and sycophancy, and had him exposed at the Jinma Ward gate.
translations.idiomatic: He also accused Wensi Hall academician, Minister of Rites, and Chengdu prefect Han Zhao of flattery and had him executed and displayed at the Jinma Ward gate.

sentences.zh: 內外馬步都指揮使兼中書令徐延瓊、果州團練使潘在迎、嘉州刺史顧在珣及諸貴戚皆惶恐，傾其家金帛妓妾以賂宗弼，僅得免死。

translations.literal: The inner and outer horse-and-foot commander-in-chief and concurrent Grand Councillor Xu Yanqiong, the Guozhou training commissioner Pan Zaiying, the Jiazhou prefect Gu Zaiqun, and various noble kin were all terrified; they poured out their households' gold, silks, singing girls, and concubines to bribe Zongbi and barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Xu Yanqiong, Guozhou commissioner Pan Zaiying, Jiazhou prefect Gu Zaiqun, and other noble kin were terrified; they emptied their households of gold, silks, and concubines to bribe Zongbi and barely escaped with their lives.

sentences.zh: 凡素所不快者，宗弼皆殺之。

translations.literal: All whom Zongbi had long disliked, he killed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone Zongbi had long resented, he killed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，繼岌至德陽。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Jiji reached Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Jiji reached Deyang.

sentences.zh: 宗弼遣使奉箋；

translations.literal: Zongbi sent envoys presenting a memorial;
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi sent envoys with a memorial;

sentences.zh: 稱已遷蜀主於西第，安撫軍城，以俟王師。

translations.literal: stating that he had already moved the Shu ruler to the western residence, pacified the garrison city, and was awaiting the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: saying he had moved the Shu ruler to the western residence, pacified the garrison city, and was awaiting the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 又使其子承班以蜀主後宮及珍玩賂繼岌及郭崇韜，求西川節度使，繼岌曰：「此皆我家物，奚以獻為！」

translations.literal: He also had his son Cheng Ban use the Shu ruler's inner palace and precious curios to bribe Jiji and Guo Chongtao, seeking the western-circuit military commission; Jiji said, "These are all my family's things—why present them as gifts!"
translations.idiomatic: He also had his son Cheng Ban offer the Shu ruler's inner palace and treasures to bribe Jiji and Guo Chongtao for the western-circuit command. Jiji said, "These are all my family's possessions—why offer them as gifts!"

sentences.zh: 留其物而遣之。

translations.literal: He kept the goods but sent the men away.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the goods but sent them away.

sentences.zh: 李紹琛留漢州八日以俟都統，甲寅，繼岌至漢州，王宗弼迎謁；

translations.literal: Li Shaochen remained at Hanzhou eight days awaiting the commander-in-chief; on jiayin Jiji reached Hanzhou and Wang Zongbi came out to welcome and pay respects;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaochen waited eight days at Hanzhou for the commander-in-chief; on jiayin Jiji reached Hanzhou, and Wang Zongbi came out to welcome him;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，至成都。

translations.literal: on yimao they reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: on yimao they entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，李嚴引蜀主及百官儀衛出降於陞遷橋，蜀主白衣、銜璧、牽羊，草繩縈首，百官衰絰、徒跣、輿櫬，號哭俟命。

translations.literal: On bingchen Li Yan led the Shu ruler and the officials with ceremonial guards out to surrender at Shengqian Bridge; the Shu ruler wore white, bore a jade disc in his mouth, led a sheep, and had a grass rope about his neck; the officials wore mourning hemp, went barefoot, and bore coffins, wailing as they awaited judgment.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Li Yan led the Shu ruler and officials with full ceremonial escort to surrender at Shengqian Bridge. The Shu ruler wore white, held a jade disc in his mouth, led a sheep, and had a grass cord about his neck; the officials wore mourning dress, went barefoot, and carried coffins, wailing as they awaited their fate.

sentences.zh: 繼岌受璧，崇韜解縛，焚櫬，承製釋罪；

translations.literal: Jiji received the jade disc; Chongtao removed the bonds, burned the coffins, and by imperial order released them from guilt;
translations.idiomatic: Jiji accepted the jade disc; Chongtao untied them, burned the coffins, and by imperial order absolved them;

sentences.zh: 君臣東北向拜謝。

translations.literal: ruler and ministers bowed in thanks toward the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: ruler and ministers bowed in thanks toward the northeast.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，大軍入成都。

translations.literal: On dingsi the great army entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the main army entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 崇韜禁軍士侵掠，市不改肆。

translations.literal: Chongtao forbade the soldiers to plunder; the markets did not change their stalls.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao forbade looting, and the markets remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 自出師至克蜀，凡七十日。

translations.literal: From the setting out of the army to the conquest of Shu, seventy days in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the army's departure to the conquest of Shu, seventy days in all.

sentences.zh: 得節度十，州六十四，縣二百四十九，兵三萬，鎧仗、錢糧、金銀、繒錦共以千萬計。

translations.literal: They gained ten military commissions, sixty-four prefectures, two hundred forty-nine counties, thirty thousand troops, and armor, weapons, money, grain, gold, silver, silks, and brocades reckoned in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: They took ten military commissions, sixty-four prefectures, two hundred forty-nine counties, thirty thousand troops, and armor, weapons, money, grain, gold, silver, silks, and brocades reckoned in the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 高季興聞蜀亡，方食，失匕箸，曰：「是老夫之過也。」

translations.literal: When Gao Jixing heard that Shu had perished, he was at his meal and dropped his spoon and chopsticks, saying, "This is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jixing heard that Shu had fallen, he was at table and dropped his spoon and chopsticks. "This is my fault," he said."

sentences.zh: 梁震曰：「不足憂也。

translations.literal: Liang Zhen said, "There is no need for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen said, "There is no need to worry.

sentences.zh: 唐主得蜀益驕，亡無日矣，安知其不為吾福！」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler, having gained Shu, will grow all the more arrogant; his fall is not far off—who knows but that this may not prove a blessing for us!"
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler, having taken Shu, will grow more arrogant still; his fall cannot be far off—who knows but that this may not turn to our advantage!"

sentences.zh: 楚王殷聞蜀亡，上表稱：「臣已營衡麓之間為菟裘之地，願上印綬以保餘齡。」

translations.literal: When King Yin of Chu heard that Shu had perished, he submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has already prepared a place between Mount Heng and Mount Lu as a retreat for his old age and wishes to surrender his seal and cord of office to preserve what years remain."
translations.idiomatic: When King Yin of Chu heard that Shu had fallen, he submitted a memorial: "Your servant has already prepared a retreat between Mount Heng and Mount Lu and wishes to surrender his seal and cord of office to live out his remaining years."

sentences.zh: 上優詔慰諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gracious edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 平蜀之功，李紹琛為多，位在董璋上。

translations.literal: In the merit of pacifying Shu, Li Shaochen's share was greatest, and his rank stood above Dong Zhang's.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaochen had done the most to pacify Shu, and his rank stood above Dong Zhang's.

sentences.zh: 而璋素與郭崇韜善，崇韜數召璋與議軍事。

translations.literal: Yet Zhang had long been on good terms with Guo Chongtao, and Chongtao repeatedly summoned Zhang to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang had long been friendly with Guo Chongtao, who repeatedly summoned him to discuss military affairs.

sentences.zh: 紹琛心不平，謂璋曰：「吾有平蜀之功，公等樸樕相從，反呫囁於郭公之門，謀相傾害。

translations.literal: Shaochen's heart was not at peace; he said to Zhang, "I have the merit of pacifying Shu, yet you rustic fellows follow along and instead whisper at Master Guo's gate, plotting to bring one another down.
translations.idiomatic: Shaochen was resentful and told Zhang, "I won Shu, yet you rustic fellows trail along and whisper at Master Guo's gate, plotting against one another.

sentences.zh: 吾為都將，獨不能以軍法斬公邪！」

translations.literal: As commander-in-chief, can I alone not execute you by military law!"
translations.idiomatic: As commander-in-chief, can I not execute you by military law!"

sentences.zh: 璋訴於崇韜。

translations.literal: Zhang complained to Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang complained to Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 十二月，崇韜表璋為東川節度使，解其軍職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chongtao memorialized that Zhang be made Dongchuan military commissioner and relieved of his army duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chongtao recommended Zhang as Dongchuan military commissioner and relieved him of his army command.

sentences.zh: 紹琛愈怒，曰：「吾冒白刃，陵險阻，定兩川，璋乃坐有之邪！」

translations.literal: Shaochen grew still angrier and said, "I braved naked blades and crossed perilous passes to settle the two circuits— and Zhang is to sit and possess it!"
translations.idiomatic: Shaochen grew angrier still. "I braved naked blades and crossed dangerous passes to settle the two circuits—and Zhang is to sit and take it!"

sentences.zh: 乃見崇韜言：「東川重地，任尚書有文武才。

translations.literal: He then saw Chongtao and said, "Dongchuan is a weighty post; Vice Minister Ren has both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Chongtao and said, "Dongchuan is a weighty post; Vice Minister Ren has both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 宜表為帥。」

translations.literal: He should be memorialized as commander."
translations.idiomatic: You should recommend him as commander."

sentences.zh: 崇韜怒曰：「紹琛反邪，何敢違吾節度！」

translations.literal: Chongtao angrily said, "Has Shaochen rebelled, that he dares defy my command!"
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao snapped, "Has Shaochen rebelled, that he dares defy my orders!"

sentences.zh: 紹琛懼而退。

translations.literal: Shaochen, afraid, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shaochen withdrew in fear.

sentences.zh: 初，帝遣宦者李從襲等從魏王繼岌伐蜀；

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent the eunuchs Li Congxi and others to follow the Prince of Wei Li Jiji in the campaign against Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent the eunuchs Li Congxi and others to accompany Prince of Wei Li Jiji in the campaign against Shu;

sentences.zh: 繼岌雖為都統，軍中制置補署一出郭崇韜，崇韜終日決事，將吏賓客趨走盈庭，而都統府惟大將晨謁外，牙門索然，從襲等固恥之。

translations.literal: though Jiji was commander-in-chief, all military arrangements and appointments in the army issued from Guo Chongtao; Chongtao decided affairs all day long, and generals, clerks, and guests hurried in and filled the court, while at the commander-in-chief's headquarters, apart from the great generals' morning audience, the gate was desolate—Congxi and the others were deeply shamed by this.
translations.idiomatic: though Jiji was commander-in-chief, every military arrangement and appointment came from Guo Chongtao. Chongtao decided affairs all day while generals, clerks, and guests crowded his hall; at the commander-in-chief's headquarters, apart from the great generals' morning audience, the gate stood empty. Congxi and the others were deeply humiliated.

sentences.zh: 及破蜀，蜀之貴臣大將爭以寶貨、妓樂遺崇韜及其子廷誨，魏王所得，不過匹馬、束帛、唾壺、麈柄而已，從襲等益不平。

translations.literal: When Shu was broken, Shu's noble ministers and great generals vied to present Chongtao and his son Tinghui with treasures, singing girls, and music; what the Prince of Wei received was no more than a horse, a bundle of silks, a spittoon, and a fly-whisk—Congxi and the others grew still more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, Shu's nobles and generals showered Chongtao and his son Tinghui with treasures, courtesans, and musicians; the Prince of Wei received nothing more than a horse, silks, a spittoon, and a fly-whisk. Congxi and the others grew still more bitter.

sentences.zh: 王宗弼之自為西川留後也，賂崇韜求為節度使，崇韜陽許之。

translations.literal: From the time Wang Zongbi had made himself acting western-circuit commissioner, he bribed Chongtao to seek the military commission; Chongtao pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Wang Zongbi had made himself acting western-circuit commissioner, he bribed Chongtao for the full commission, and Chongtao pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 既而久未得，乃帥蜀人列狀見繼岌，請留崇韜鎮蜀。

translations.literal: After a long while he still had not obtained it; he then led the Shu people in submitting a joint petition to Jiji asking that Chongtao be kept to govern Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When he still had not received it after a long wait, he led the Shu people in a joint petition to Jiji asking that Chongtao be left to govern Shu.

sentences.zh: 從襲等因謂繼岌曰：「郭公父子專橫，今又使蜀人請己為帥，其志難測，王不可不為備。」

translations.literal: Congxi and the others thereupon said to Jiji, "Master Guo and his son act arbitrarily; now they have had the Shu people ask that he be made commander—their intentions are hard to fathom; Your Highness must take precautions."
translations.idiomatic: Congxi and the others then told Jiji, "Master Guo and his son are running everything; now they have had the Shu people ask that he be made commander—their intentions are hard to read. Your Highness must be on guard."

sentences.zh: 繼岌謂崇韜曰：「主上倚侍中如山嶽，不可離廟堂，豈肯棄元臣於蠻夷之域乎！

translations.literal: Jiji said to Chongtao, "Our lord relies on the Chief Councillor as on mountains and cliffs; he cannot leave the court—would he abandon a founding minister in the land of barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: Jiji told Chongtao, "Our lord relies on the Chief Councillor as on mountains and cliffs; he cannot leave the court—would he abandon a founding minister in barbarian lands!

sentences.zh: 且此非余之所敢知也，請諸人詣闕自陳。」

translations.literal: Moreover this is not something I dare decide; let the petitioners go to the capital and state it themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, this is not for me to decide; let the petitioners go to court and speak for themselves."

sentences.zh: 由是繼岌與崇韜互相疑。

translations.literal: From this Jiji and Chongtao came to suspect each other.
translations.idiomatic: From this Jiji and Chongtao began to mistrust each other.

sentences.zh: 會宋光葆自梓州來，訴王宗弼誣殺宋光嗣等。

translations.literal: Just then Song Guangbao came from Zizhou and accused Wang Zongbi of falsely killing Song Guangsi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Song Guangbao arrived from Zizhou and accused Wang Zongbi of falsely killing Song Guangsi and the others.

sentences.zh: 又，崇韜征犒軍錢數萬緡於宗弼，宗弼靳之，士卒怨怒，夜，縱火喧噪。

translations.literal: Moreover Chongtao levied several tens of thousands of strings in army-reward money from Zongbi; Zongbi was stingy with it, and the soldiers were resentful and angry; at night they set fires and raised an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao also demanded tens of thousands of strings in reward money from Zongbi; Zongbi refused to pay, and the soldiers grew angry. That night they set fires and raised an uproar.

sentences.zh: 崇韜欲誅宗弼以自明，己巳，白繼岌收宗弼及王宗勳、王宗渥，皆數其不忠之罪，族誅之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Chongtao wished to execute Zongbi to clear himself; on jisi he reported to Jiji to seize Zongbi together with Wang Zongxun and Wang Zongwo, counted out their crimes of disloyalty, executed their entire clans, and confiscated their households.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao wanted to execute Zongbi to clear himself. On jisi he asked Jiji to seize Zongbi along with Wang Zongxun and Wang Zongwo, charged them with disloyalty, executed their entire clans, and confiscated their property.

sentences.zh: 蜀人爭食宗弼之肉。

translations.literal: The Shu people vied to eat Zongbi's flesh.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu fought over Zongbi's flesh.

sentences.zh: 辛未，閩忠懿王審知卒，子延翰自稱威武留後。

translations.literal: On xinwei the Loyal and Sagacious King of Min Wang Shenzhi died; his son Yanhan styled himself acting Weiwu commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Loyal and Sagacious King of Min Wang Shenzhi died; his son Yanhan declared himself acting Weiwu commissioner.

sentences.zh: 汀州民陳本聚眾三萬圍汀州，延翰遣右軍都監柳邕等將兵二萬討之。

translations.literal: Chen Ben of Tingzhou gathered thirty thousand men and besieged Tingzhou; Yanhan sent the right-army inspector Liu Yong and others to lead twenty thousand troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ben of Tingzhou raised thirty thousand men and besieged Tingzhou; Yanhan sent right-army inspector Liu Yong and others with twenty thousand troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，王承休、王宗汭至成都，魏王繼岌詰之曰：「居大鎮，擁強兵，何以不拒戰？」

translations.literal: On guiyou Wang Chengxiu and Wang Zongrui reached Chengdu; the Prince of Wei Li Jiji questioned them, saying, "You held a great command and possessed strong troops—why did you not resist in battle?"
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Wang Chengxiu and Wang Zongrui reached Chengdu. Prince of Wei Li Jiji questioned them: "You held a great command and strong troops—why did you not fight?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「畏大王神武。」

translations.literal: They answered, "We feared Your Highness's divine martial prowess."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We feared Your Highness's martial prowess."

sentences.zh: 曰：「然則何不降？」

translations.literal: He said, "Then why did you not surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Then why did you not surrender?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「王師不入境。」

translations.literal: They answered, "The royal army had not entered our territory."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The imperial army had not yet entered our territory."

sentences.zh: 曰：「所俱入羌者幾人？」

translations.literal: He said, "How many went with you into the Qiang lands?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "How many went with you into Qiang territory?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「萬二千人。」

translations.literal: They answered, "Twelve thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Twelve thousand men."

sentences.zh: 曰：「今歸者幾人？」

translations.literal: He said, "How many have returned now?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "How many have returned now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「二千人。」

translations.literal: They answered, "Two thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Two thousand men."

sentences.zh: 曰：「可以償萬人之死矣。」

translations.literal: He said, "That may answer for the deaths of ten thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "That will answer for the deaths of ten thousand men."

sentences.zh: 皆斬之，並其子。

translations.literal: All were beheaded, together with their sons.
translations.idiomatic: All were executed, together with their sons.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以知北都留守事孟知祥為西川節度使、同平章事，促召赴洛陽。

translations.literal: On bingzi Meng Zhixiang, who was administering the northern capital in the emperor's stead, was made western-circuit military commissioner and concurrent Chief Councillor, and urgently summoned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Meng Zhixiang, administrator of the northern capital, was appointed western-circuit military commissioner and concurrent Chief Councillor and urgently summoned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝議選北都留守，樞密承旨段徊等惡鄴都留守張憲，不欲其在朝廷，皆曰：「北都非張憲不可。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed choosing a northern-capital administrator; Privy Council director Duan Huai and others disliked Ye capital administrator Zhang Xian and did not want him at court; all said, "For the northern capital no one but Zhang Xian will do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed choosing a northern-capital administrator. Privy Council director Duan Huai and others disliked Ye capital administrator Zhang Xian and did not want him at court; all said, "Only Zhang Xian will do for the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 憲雖有宰相器，今國家新得中原，宰相在天子目前，事有得失，可以改更，比之此都獨系一方安危，不為重也。」

translations.literal: Though Xian has the makings of a chief councillor, the state has newly gained the central plain; a chief councillor is before the Son of Heaven's very eyes, and when affairs go wrong they can be changed—compared with this capital, on which the safety of a whole region alone depends, that is not as weighty."
translations.idiomatic: Though Xian has the makings of a chief councillor, the state has just taken the central plain; a chief councillor stands before the Son of Heaven, and mistakes can be corrected—whereas this capital alone holds the safety of a whole region, which matters more."

sentences.zh: 乃徙憲為太原尹，知北都留守事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xian was transferred to be Taiyuan prefect and administer the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was therefore transferred to Taiyuan prefect and made administrator of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書王正言為興唐尹，知鄴都留守事。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Wang Zhengyan was made Xingtang prefect and administered the Ye capital.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Wang Zhengyan was made Xingtang prefect and administrator of the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 正言昏耄，帝以武德使史彥瓊為鄴都監軍。

translations.literal: Zhengyan was senile; the emperor made Wude commissioner Shi Yanqiong Ye-capital military overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan was senile, so the emperor made Wude commissioner Shi Yanqiong military overseer of the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 彥瓊，本伶人也，有寵於帝。

translations.literal: Yanqiong had originally been an actor and enjoyed the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiong had originally been an actor and enjoyed the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 魏、博等六州軍旅金谷之政皆決於彥瓊，威福自恣，陵忽將佐，自正言以下皆諂事之。

translations.literal: The military and fiscal affairs of the six prefectures Wei, Bo, and the rest were all decided by Yanqiong; he wielded power as he pleased, looked down on generals and aides, and from Zhengyan downward all flattered and served him.
translations.idiomatic: Military and fiscal affairs for the six prefectures of Wei, Bo, and the rest all fell to Yanqiong; he wielded power as he pleased, looked down on officers, and from Zhengyan downward everyone flattered him.

sentences.zh: 初，帝得魏州銀槍效節都近八千人，以為親軍，皆恿悍無敵。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had obtained nearly eight thousand men of the Yinqian Xiaojie command at Weizhou and made them his personal army; all were fierce and matchless.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had taken nearly eight thousand men of the Silver Spear Xiaojie command at Weizhou as his personal army; all were fierce and matchless.

sentences.zh: 夾河之戰，實賴其用，屢立殊功，常許以滅梁之日大加賞賚。

translations.literal: In the battles along the Yellow River they had truly been relied upon, repeatedly winning extraordinary merit; he had often promised that on the day Liang was destroyed they would be greatly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: In the battles along the Yellow River they had proved indispensable and won repeated distinction; he had often promised that when Liang fell they would be richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 既而河南平，雖賞賚非一，而士卒恃功，驕恣無厭，更成怨望。

translations.literal: After Henan was pacified, though rewards were not few, the soldiers relied on their merit, grew arrogant and insatiable, and turned instead to resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After Henan was pacified, rewards came again and again, yet the soldiers, trusting in their merit, grew arrogant and insatiable and turned to resentment instead.

sentences.zh: 是歲大饑多流亡，租賦不充，道路塗潦，漕輦艱澀，東都倉廩空竭，無以給軍士。

translations.literal: That year there was great famine and many fled; rents and levies were not filled; roads were mired; transport by water was difficult; the eastern capital's granaries were empty and exhausted, and there was nothing with which to supply the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine drove many to flee; taxes went uncollected; roads were mired and river transport stalled; the eastern capital's granaries stood empty, and there was nothing with which to pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 租唐使孔謙日於上東門外望諸州漕運，至者隨以給之。

translations.literal: The Rent-Tang commissioner Kong Qian daily watched at the Upper East Gate for transport from the prefectures and, as it arrived, issued it forthwith.
translations.idiomatic: Rent-Tang commissioner Kong Qian waited daily at the Upper East Gate for grain shipments from the prefectures and issued whatever arrived on the spot.

sentences.zh: 軍士乏食，有雇妻鬻子者，老弱采蔬於野，百十為群，往往餒死，流言怨嗟，而帝游畋不息。

translations.literal: The soldiers lacked food; some hired out their wives or sold their children; the old and weak gathered vegetables in the wild in groups of a hundred or ten, and often starved to death; rumors and complaints spread, yet the emperor's hunting excursions did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The troops went hungry; some hired out their wives or sold their children; the old and weak gathered wild vegetables in bands of dozens and often starved; murmurs of resentment spread, yet the emperor kept hunting without pause.

sentences.zh: 己卯，獵於白沙，皇后，皇子、後宮畢從。

translations.literal: On jimao he hunted at Baisha; the empress, princes, and inner palace all followed.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he hunted at Baisha, with the empress, princes, and entire inner palace in attendance.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，宿伊闕；

translations.literal: On gengchen he lodged at Yique;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he lodged at Yique;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，宿潭泊；

translations.literal: on xinsi he lodged at Tanbo;
translations.idiomatic: on xinsi he lodged at Tanbo;

sentences.zh: 壬午，宿龕澗；

translations.literal: on renwu he lodged at Kanjian;
translations.idiomatic: on renwu he lodged at Kanjian;

sentences.zh: 癸未，還宮。

translations.literal: on guiwei he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on guiwei he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 時大雪，吏座有僵仆於道路者。

translations.literal: Snow fell heavily; among the officials' retinues some collapsed rigid in the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell heavily, and some of the officials' attendants collapsed dead in the roads.

sentences.zh: 伊、汝間饑尤甚，衛兵所過，責其供餉，不得，則壞其什器，撤其室廬以為薪，甚於寇盜，縣吏皆竄匿山谷。

translations.literal: Between the Yi and Ru rivers famine was especially severe; wherever the palace guards passed they demanded provisions, and if they did not recover them they smashed utensils and tore down houses for firewood—worse than bandits—and county clerks all fled and hid in the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Famine was worst between the Yi and Ru rivers. Wherever palace guards passed they demanded supplies; when refused they smashed goods and tore down houses for firewood, behaving worse than bandits, and county clerks fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 有白龍見於漢宮；

translations.literal: A white dragon was seen in the Han palace;
translations.idiomatic: A white dragon was seen in the Han palace;

sentences.zh: 漢主改元白龍，更名曰龔。

translations.literal: the Han ruler changed the era name to Bailong and renamed himself Gong.
translations.idiomatic: the Han ruler changed the era name to Bailong and took the personal name Gong.

sentences.zh: 長和驃信鄭旻遣其布燮鄭昭淳求婚於漢，漢主以女增城公主妻之。

translations.literal: The Changhe commander-in-chief Zheng Min sent his minister Zheng Zhaochun to seek marriage with Han; the Han ruler gave his daughter Princess Zengcheng in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Changhe commander-in-chief Zheng Min sent minister Zheng Zhaochun to seek a marriage alliance with Han; the Han ruler gave his daughter Princess Zengcheng as bride.

sentences.zh: 長和即唐之南詔也。

translations.literal: Changhe was Tang's Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Changhe was Tang's Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使李嗣源入朝。

translations.literal: The Chengde military commissioner Li Siyuan entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde military commissioner Li Siyuan came to court.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己丑朔，孟知祥至洛陽，帝寵待甚厚。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the jichou new moon, Meng Zhixiang reached Luoyang and the emperor favored and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the jichou new moon, Meng Zhixiang reached Luoyang, where the emperor received him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 帝以軍儲不足，謀於群臣，豆盧革以下皆莫知為計。

translations.literal: Because military stores were insufficient, the emperor consulted the ministers; Doulu Ge and those below all knew no plan.
translations.idiomatic: With military stores running short, the emperor consulted his ministers, but Doulu Ge and the rest could offer no plan.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李琪上疏，以為：「古者量入以為出，計農而發兵，故雖有水旱之災而無匱乏之憂。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Qi submitted a memorial saying, "In antiquity one measured income to determine expenditure and counted the harvest before raising troops; therefore though there were flood and drought disasters there was no fear of want.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Li Qi submitted a memorial arguing that "in antiquity rulers measured income before spending and counted the harvest before raising armies, so that even flood and drought brought no fear of shortage.

sentences.zh: 近代稅農以養兵，未有農富給而兵不足，農捐瘠而兵豐飽者也。

translations.literal: In recent times the peasantry is taxed to feed the army; never yet has the peasantry been rich and ample while the army was insufficient, or the peasantry wasted and lean while the army was full and fed.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the peasantry is taxed to feed the army; never yet have farmers been prosperous while troops went hungry, or farmers been impoverished while soldiers were well fed.

sentences.zh: 今縱未能蠲省租稅，苟除折納、紐配之法，農亦可以小休矣。」

translations.literal: Now even if we cannot yet reduce or lighten rents and taxes, if we merely abolish the methods of conversion payments and forced substitution, the farmers may also gain a little rest."
translations.idiomatic: Even if rents cannot yet be cut, abolishing conversion payments and forced substitution would at least give farmers some relief."

sentences.zh: 帝即敕有司如琪所言，然竟不能行。

translations.literal: The emperor at once ordered the responsible offices to act as Qi had said, yet in the end it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered the responsible offices to follow Qi's advice, but in the end nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔蜀朝所署官四品以上降授有差，五品以下才地無取者悉縱歸田裡；

translations.literal: On dingyou an edict ordered that officials appointed by the Shu court of the fourth rank and above be demoted and reassigned with distinctions, while those of the fifth rank and below who lacked talent and standing were all released to return to their villages;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou an edict demoted former Shu officials of the fourth rank and above with varying degrees of severity and released fifth-rank officials and below who lacked merit to return home;

sentences.zh: 其先降及有功者，委崇韜隨事獎任。

translations.literal: those who had surrendered earlier and those with merit were entrusted to Chongtao to reward and appoint according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: those who had surrendered early or rendered merit were left to Chongtao to reward and appoint as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 又賜王衍詔，略曰：「固當襲土而封，必不薄人於險。

translations.literal: He also bestowed an edict on Wang Yan, which in summary said, "You shall surely receive a fief and enfeoffment; I will certainly not treat a man harshly in his peril.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Wang Yan an edict that read in part, "You shall receive a fief and enfeoffment; I will not treat a man harshly in his distress.

sentences.zh: 三辰在上，一言不欺。」

translations.literal: With sun, moon, and stars above, not one word shall deceive."
translations.idiomatic: With sun, moon, and stars as witness, not one word shall prove false."

sentences.zh: 庚子，彰武、保大節度使兼史書令高萬興卒，以其子保大留後允韜為彰武留後。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Zhangwu and Baoda military commissioner and concurrent Director of the History Bureau Gao Wanxing died; his son Baoda acting commissioner Yuntao was made Zhangwu acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Zhangwu and Baoda military commissioner Gao Wanxing, who also held the post of Director of the History Bureau, died; his son Yuntao, acting commissioner of Baoda, was made acting commissioner of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 帝以軍儲不充，欲如汴州，諫官上言：「不如節儉以足用，自古無就食天子。

translations.literal: Because military stores were not full, the emperor wished to go to Bianzhou; remonstrating officials submitted, "It would be better to practice frugality to make supplies suffice; from antiquity there has never been a Son of Heaven who went to eat elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: With military stores depleted, the emperor wished to go to Bianzhou; remonstrating officials urged, "Better to practice frugality than to move the court; never in history has a Son of Heaven gone elsewhere to be fed.

sentences.zh: 今楊氏未滅，不宜示以虛實。」

translations.literal: Now the Yang house is not yet destroyed; it is not fitting to reveal our strength or weakness."
translations.idiomatic: The Yang regime is not yet destroyed; we should not reveal our weakness."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，立皇弟存美為邕王，存霸為永王，存禮為薛王，存渥為申王，存又為睦王，存確為通王，存紀為雅王。

translations.literal: On xinhai the emperor's younger brothers were enfeoffed: Cunmei as Prince of Yong, Cunba as Prince of Yong, Cunli as Prince of Xue, Cunwo as Prince of Shen, Cunyou as Prince of Mu, Cunque as Prince of Tong, and Cunji as Prince of Ya.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor enfeoffed his younger brothers: Cunmei as Prince of Yong, Cunba as Prince of Yong, Cunli as Prince of Xue, Cunwo as Prince of Shen, Cunyou as Prince of Mu, Cunque as Prince of Tong, and Cunji as Prince of Ya.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜素疾宦官，嘗密謂魏王繼岌曰：「大王他日得天下，騬馬亦不可乘，況任宦官！

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao had long detested eunuchs and once secretly told the Prince of Wei Li Jiji, "When Your Highness one day gains the realm, even a gelded horse may not be ridden—how much less should eunuchs be employed!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao had long hated eunuchs and once told Prince of Wei Li Jiji in private, "When Your Highness one day rules the realm, even a gelded horse should not be ridden—how much less should eunuchs hold office!

sentences.zh: 宜盡去之，專用士人。」

translations.literal: They should all be removed and only scholar-officials employed."
translations.idiomatic: Remove them all and employ only scholar-officials."

sentences.zh: 呂知柔竊聽，聞之，由是宦官皆切齒。

translations.literal: Lü Zhirou overheard in secret; when he heard it, from this the eunuchs all gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhirou overheard this in secret, and from then on the eunuchs gnashed their teeth against Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 時成都雖下，而蜀中盜賊群起，佈滿山林。

translations.literal: At that time though Chengdu had fallen, bandits rose in groups throughout Shu and filled the mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chengdu had fallen, bandits rose throughout Shu and filled the hills.

sentences.zh: 崇韜恐大軍既去，更為後患，命任圜、張筠分道招討，以是淹留未還。

translations.literal: Chongtao feared that once the great army departed they would become a later calamity and ordered Ren Huan and Zhang Jun to pursue and pacify them by separate routes; for this reason he lingered and had not returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao feared that once the main army left, the bandits would become a lasting threat, so he ordered Ren Huan and Zhang Jun to pacify them by separate routes and lingered in Shu.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宦者向延嗣促之，崇韜不出郊迎，及見，禮節又倨，延嗣怒。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to urge him on; Chongtao did not go out to the suburbs to welcome him, and when they met his courtesy was again arrogant—Yansi was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuch Xiang Yansi to hurry him along. Chongtao did not go out to welcome him, and when they met his manner was arrogant; Yansi was furious.

sentences.zh: 李從襲謂延嗣曰：「魏王，太子也；

translations.literal: Li Congxi said to Yansi, "The Prince of Wei is the heir;
translations.idiomatic: Li Congxi told Yansi, "The Prince of Wei is the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 主上萬福，而郭公專權如是。

translations.literal: our lord enjoys ten thousand blessings, yet Master Guo monopolizes power like this.
translations.idiomatic: our lord enjoys every blessing, yet Master Guo wields power like this.

sentences.zh: 郭廷誨擁徒出入，日與軍中饒將、蜀土豪傑狎飲，指天畫地，近聞白其父請表己為蜀帥；

translations.literal: Guo Tinghui goes in and out with a crowd of followers, daily drinking familiarly with the army's senior generals and Shu's local magnates, pointing to heaven and tracing on the ground; recently it was heard that he told his father to memorialize requesting that he himself be made Shu commander;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tinghui goes about with a retinue, drinking daily with senior generals and Shu magnates, boasting extravagantly; lately it is said he urged his father to memorialize asking that he be made commander of Shu;

sentences.zh: 又言『蜀地富饒，大人宜善自為謀。』

translations.literal: and also said, 'Shu is rich and fertile; my lord ought to plan well for himself.'
translations.idiomatic: and said, 'Shu is rich; Father ought to look to his own interests.'

sentences.zh: 今諸軍將校皆郭氏之黨，王寄身於虎狼之口，一委有變，吾屬不知委骨何地矣。」

translations.literal: Now all the army's officers are Guo clique men; the Prince lodges his person in the mouths of tigers and wolves—if anything goes wrong, we do not know where our bones will be cast."
translations.idiomatic: Now every officer is a Guo partisan; the Prince stands among wolves—if anything goes wrong, we will not know where our bones will lie."

sentences.zh: 因相向垂涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon they faced one another and wept.
translations.idiomatic: They faced one another and wept.

sentences.zh: 延嗣歸，具以語劉後。

translations.literal: Yansi returned and reported it all to Empress Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Yansi returned and reported everything to Empress Liu.

sentences.zh: 後泣訴於帝，請早救繼岌之死。

translations.literal: The empress wept and pleaded before the emperor, asking that Jiji be saved from death while there was still time.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept before the emperor and begged him to save Jiji before it was too late.

sentences.zh: 前此帝聞蜀人請崇韜為帥，已不平，至是聞延嗣之言，不能無疑。

translations.literal: Earlier when the emperor had heard that the Shu people asked that Chongtao be made commander, he was already displeased; now, hearing Yansi's words, he could not be without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already been displeased when he heard the Shu people wanted Chongtao as commander; now Yansi's report left him deeply suspicious.

sentences.zh: 帝閱蜀府庫之籍，曰：「人言蜀中珍貨無算，何如是之微也？」

translations.literal: The emperor examined the Shu treasury registers and said, "People say the treasures of Shu are beyond counting—why are they so slight?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor examined the Shu treasury registers and said, "People say Shu held untold treasures—why is the tally so small?"

sentences.zh: 延嗣曰：「臣聞蜀破，其珍貨皆入於崇韜父子，崇韜有金萬兩，銀四十萬兩，錢百萬緡，名馬千匹，他物稱是，廷誨所取，復在其外；

translations.literal: Yansi said, "Your servant heard that when Shu was broken, its treasures all entered Chongtao and his son; Chongtao has ten thousand taels of gold, four hundred thousand taels of silver, a million strings of cash, a thousand famous horses, and other goods in proportion—what Tinghui took is again beyond this;
translations.idiomatic: Yansi said, "I hear that when Shu fell, the treasures went to Chongtao and his son. Chongtao alone has ten thousand taels of gold, four hundred thousand taels of silver, a million strings of cash, a thousand fine horses, and goods to match—and Tinghui's share is on top of that;

sentences.zh: 故縣官所得不多耳。」

translations.literal: therefore what the state treasury obtained was not much."
translations.idiomatic: so the state treasury received little."

sentences.zh: 帝遂怒形於色。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger then showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 及孟知祥將行，帝語之曰：「聞郭崇韜有異志，卿到，為朕誅之。」

translations.literal: When Meng Zhixiang was about to depart, the emperor told him, "I hear Guo Chongtao has rebellious intentions; when you arrive, execute him for me."
translations.idiomatic: As Meng Zhixiang was about to leave, the emperor told him, "I hear Guo Chongtao harbors rebellious intentions. When you arrive, put him to death for me."

sentences.zh: 知祥曰：「崇韜，國之勳舊，不宜有此。

translations.literal: Zhixiang said, "Chongtao is an old meritorious servant of the state; he ought not to have this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang said, "Chongtao is a founding minister of the state; he should not be capable of this.

sentences.zh: 俟臣至蜀察之，苟無他志則遣還。」

translations.literal: Wait until your servant reaches Shu and investigates; if he has no other intent, send him back."
translations.idiomatic: Let me reach Shu and investigate; if he has no other intent, send him home."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬子，知祥發洛陽。

translations.literal: On renzi Zhixiang departed from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Zhixiang left Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝尋復遣衣甲庫使馬彥珪馳詣成都觀崇韜去就，如奉詔班師則已，若有遷延跋扈之狀，則與繼岌圖之。

translations.literal: The emperor soon again sent the wardrobe-and-armor-store commissioner Ma Yan'gui in haste to Chengdu to observe Chongtao's going and staying; if he obeyed the edict and withdrew the army, that would be enough, but if there were signs of delay and arrogance, he was to plot with Jiji against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon sent wardrobe-and-armor-store commissioner Ma Yan'gui posthaste to Chengdu to watch Chongtao. If Chongtao obeyed orders and withdrew, so be it; if he delayed or acted arrogantly, Yan'gui was to plot with Jiji against him.

sentences.zh: 彥珪見皇后，說之曰：「臣見向延嗣言蜀中事勢憂在朝夕，今上當斷不斷，夫成敗之機，間不容髮，安能緩急稟命於三千里外乎！」

translations.literal: Yan'gui saw the empress and urged her, saying, "Your servant heard Xiang Yansi say that the situation in Shu is critical within days; the present emperor ought to decide but does not. The moment of success or failure allows no hair's breadth between—how can one report urgently or slowly to await orders three thousand li away!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan'gui saw the empress and urged, "Xiang Yansi says the crisis in Shu may come any day. The emperor hesitates when he should act. Success and failure hang by a thread—how can we wait for orders from three thousand li away!"

sentences.zh: 皇后復言於帝，帝曰：「傳聞之言，未知虛實，豈可遽爾果決？」

translations.literal: The empress spoke again to the emperor; the emperor said, "These are rumors—we do not know truth from falsehood; how can we suddenly make a firm decision?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress spoke to the emperor again. He said, "These are rumors—we do not know what is true. How can we act on them so hastily?"

sentences.zh: 皇后不得請，退，自為教與繼岌，令殺崇韜。

translations.literal: The empress could not obtain her request; she withdrew and herself drafted an order for Jiji commanding that Chongtao be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress could not persuade him. She withdrew and drafted her own order to Jiji commanding Chongtao's death.

sentences.zh: 知祥行至石壕，彥珪夜叩門宣詔，促知祥赴鎮，知祥竊歎曰：「亂將作矣！」

translations.literal: When Zhixiang reached Shihao, Yan'gui knocked at the gate by night to proclaim the edict, urging Zhixiang to hurry to his post; Zhixiang sighed privately and said, "Trouble is about to break out!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang reached Shihao, Yan'gui knocked at his door at night with the edict, urging him to hurry to his post. Zhixiang sighed to himself, "Trouble is coming!"

sentences.zh: 乃晝夜兼行。

translations.literal: He then traveled day and night without pause.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on day and night.

sentences.zh: 初，楚王殷既得湖南，不征商旅，由是四方商旅輻水奏。

translations.literal: Earlier, when King Yin of Chu had gained Hunan, he did not tax merchants and travelers; from this merchants and travelers from all quarters converged like spokes to a hub.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when King Yin of Chu took Hunan, he levied no taxes on merchants, and travelers from every direction converged on the region.

sentences.zh: 湖南地多鉛鐵，殷用軍都判官高郁策，鑄鉛鐵為錢，商旅出境，無所用之，皆易他貨而去，故能以境內所餘之物易天下百貨，國以富饒。

translations.literal: Hunan had much lead and iron; Yin employed the army director's aide Gao Yu's plan to cast lead and iron as coin; when merchants left the borders they had no use for it and all exchanged it for other goods and departed; thus he could trade the surplus goods within his borders for all the goods under heaven, and the state grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had abundant lead and iron. Yin followed army director's aide Gao Yu's plan and cast lead-iron coin. Merchants leaving the border could not use it elsewhere and traded it for other goods, so Chu exchanged its surplus for goods from across the realm and grew rich.

sentences.zh: 湖南民不事桑蠶，郁命民輸稅者皆以帛代錢，未幾，民間機杼大盛。

translations.literal: The people of Hunan did not engage in mulberry and silkworm cultivation; Yu ordered that those paying taxes all use silk cloth in place of cash; before long, looms flourished greatly among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Hunan did not raise silkworms. Yu required tax payments in silk cloth instead of coin, and before long weaving flourished throughout the countryside.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐遣使者沈□致書，以受玉冊，封吳越國王告於吳。

translations.literal: The King of Wuyue Qian Liu sent the envoy Shen [character missing] with a letter announcing that he had received the jade book and been enfeoffed King of Wuyue, to inform Wu.
translations.idiomatic: King of Wuyue Qian Liu sent envoy Shen [character missing] with a letter announcing his receipt of the jade book and enfeoffment as King of Wuyue, to inform Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳人以其國名與己同，不受書，遣□還。

translations.literal: The people of Wu, because their state's name was the same as their own, did not accept the letter and sent [him] back.
translations.idiomatic: Wu refused the letter because its state's name matched their own and sent the envoy back.

sentences.zh: 仍戒境上無得通吳越使者及商旅。

translations.literal: They also warned the border that Wuyue envoys and merchants must not be allowed passage.
translations.idiomatic: They also forbade Wuyue envoys and merchants from crossing the border.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong Shengde Hewu Qinxiao, Part One, Upper
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong Shengde Hewu Qinxiao, Part One, Upper

sentences.zh: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝下天成元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong Guangsheng Shenmin Xiaoxiao, Lower, Tiancheng year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang, Tiancheng year 1 (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元九二六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, AD 926)
translations.idiomatic: bingxu, AD 926)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚申，魏王繼岌遣李繼曮、李嚴部送王衍及其宗族百官數千人詣洛陽。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengshen, the Prince of Wei Li Jiji sent Li Jiyong and Li Yan to escort Wang Yan and his clan, officials, and several thousand men to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengshen, Prince of Wei Li Jiji sent Li Jiyong and Li Yan to escort Wang Yan, his clan, and several thousand officials to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使、尚書令李繼麟自恃與帝故舊，且有功，帝待之厚，苦諸伶宦求丐無厭，遂拒不與。

translations.literal: The Hezhong military commissioner and Minister of Works Li Jilin relied on his old friendship with the emperor and on his merit; the emperor treated him generously, but he suffered from the actors and eunuchs begging without end and therefore refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong military commissioner and Minister of Works Li Jilin relied on his old ties with the emperor and on his merit; though the emperor treated him generously, he grew weary of endless demands from actors and eunuchs and refused them.

sentences.zh: 大軍之征蜀也，繼麟閱兵，遣其子令德將之以從。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Shu, Jilin reviewed troops and sent his son Lingde to lead them in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched against Shu, Jilin reviewed his troops and sent his son Lingde to lead them in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 景進與宦官譖之曰：「繼麟聞大軍起，以為討己，故驚懼，閱兵自衛。」

translations.literal: Jing Jin and the eunuchs slandered him, saying, "Jilin heard the great army rise and thought it was to attack him; therefore he was alarmed and reviewed troops to guard himself."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Jin and the eunuchs slandered him, saying, "Jilin heard the army was marching and thought it was aimed at him, so in alarm he reviewed troops to defend himself."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「崇韜所以敢倔強於蜀者，與河中陰謀，內外相應故也。」

translations.literal: They also said, "The reason Chongtao dares to be stubborn in Shu is that he plots secretly with Hezhong and they respond to each other within and without."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "Chongtao dares act arrogantly in Shu because he is plotting secretly with Hezhong, coordinating inside and out."

sentences.zh: 繼麟聞之懼，欲身入朝以自明，其所親止之，繼麟曰：「郭侍中功高於我。

translations.literal: When Jilin heard this he was afraid and wished to enter court in person to clear himself; those close to him stopped him. Jilin said, "Chief Councillor Guo's merit is higher than mine.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin was afraid and wished to go to court in person to clear himself, but his intimates stopped him. Jilin said, "Chief Councillor Guo's merit exceeds mine.

sentences.zh: 今事勢將危，吾得見主上，面陳至誠，則讒人獲罪矣。」

translations.literal: Now the situation is about to turn dangerous; if I can see our lord and state my utmost sincerity face to face, then the slanderers will be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Now the situation is turning dangerous. If I can see our lord face to face and speak with full sincerity, the slanderers will be punished."

sentences.zh: 癸亥，繼麟入朝。

translations.literal: On guihai Jilin entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Jilin came to court.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌將發成都，令任圜權知留事，以俟孟知祥。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei Li Jiji was about to depart Chengdu; he ordered Ren Huan to administer remaining affairs in the emperor's stead, to await Meng Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Li Jiji was about to leave Chengdu. He left Ren Huan in charge of affairs until Meng Zhixiang arrived.

sentences.zh: 諸軍部署已定，是日，馬彥珪至，以皇后教示繼岌，繼岌曰：「大軍垂發，彼無釁端，安可為此負心事！

translations.literal: All the armies' deployments were settled; that day Ma Yan'gui arrived and showed Jiji the empress's order. Jiji said, "The great army is on the verge of departure; he has given no cause—how can we do this shameful deed!
translations.idiomatic: The army was ready to march when Ma Yan'gui arrived with the empress's order. Jiji said, "The army is about to depart and he has given no cause—how can we commit this shameful act!

sentences.zh: 公輩勿復言。

translations.literal: You gentlemen, speak no more of it.
translations.idiomatic: Say no more of it.

sentences.zh: 且主上無敕，獨以皇后教殺招討使，可乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover our lord has issued no edict—can we alone, on the empress's order, kill the expedition commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, our lord has issued no edict—can we kill the expedition commissioner on the empress's order alone?"

sentences.zh: 李從襲等泣曰：「既有此跡，萬一崇韜聞之，中塗為變，益不可救矣。」

translations.literal: Li Congxi and the others wept and said, "Since there is already this trace of intent, if by chance Chongtao hears of it and makes trouble midway, it will be still less possible to save the situation."
translations.idiomatic: Li Congxi and the others wept and said, "Since suspicion already exists, if Chongtao hears of this and rebels on the road, nothing can save us."

sentences.zh: 相與巧陳利害，繼岌不得已從之。

translations.literal: They together artfully set forth advantage and harm, and Jiji, having no choice, followed them.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed their case artfully, and Jiji, having no choice, agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲子旦，從襲以繼岌之命召崇韜計事，繼岌登樓避之。

translations.literal: At dawn on jiazi Congxi, by Jiji's command, summoned Chongtao to discuss affairs; Jiji ascended a tower to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jiazi Congxi summoned Chongtao on Jiji's orders to discuss affairs; Jiji went up a tower to avoid the scene.

sentences.zh: 崇韜方升階，繼岌從者李環撾碎其首，並殺其子廷誨、廷信。

translations.literal: As Chongtao was just mounting the steps, Jiji's follower Li Huan smashed his skull, and his sons Tinghui and Tingxin were killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: As Chongtao mounted the steps, Jiji's follower Li Huan smashed his skull; his sons Tinghui and Tingxin were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 外人猶未之知。

translations.literal: Those outside still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Those outside still knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 都統推官饒陽李崧謂繼岌曰：「今行軍三千里外，初無敕旨，擅殺大將，大王奈何行此危事！

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief's aide Raoyang Li Song said to Jiji, "Now the army marches three thousand li away; there was originally no edict, yet a great general has been killed on our own authority—how can Your Highness do this dangerous deed!
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief's aide Li Song of Raoyang told Jiji, "The army is three thousand li from home with no imperial order, yet you have killed a great general on your own authority—how can Your Highness do this!

sentences.zh: 獨不能忍之至洛陽邪？」

translations.literal: Could you not alone have borne with it until Luoyang?"
translations.idiomatic: Could you not have waited until Luoyang?"

sentences.zh: 繼岌曰：「公言是也，悔之無及。」

translations.literal: Jiji said, "Your words are right; regret is of no avail."
translations.idiomatic: Jiji said, "You are right. It is too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 崧乃召書吏數人，登樓去梯，矯為敕書，用蠟印宣之，軍中粗定。

translations.literal: Song then summoned several clerks, ascended the tower and removed the ladder, forged an edict, sealed it with wax, and proclaimed it; the army was roughly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Song summoned several clerks, went up the tower and removed the ladder, forged an edict, sealed it with wax, and proclaimed it; the army was roughly calmed.

sentences.zh: 崇韜左右皆竄匿，獨掌書記滏陽張礪詣魏王府慟哭久之。

translations.literal: Chongtao's attendants all fled and hid; only his secretary Fuyang Zhang Li went to the Prince of Wei's residence and wept long in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao's attendants all fled; only his secretary Zhang Li of Fuyang went to the Prince of Wei's residence and wept long.

sentences.zh: 繼岌命任圜代崇韜總軍政。

translations.literal: Jiji ordered Ren Huan to replace Chongtao in overall military and civil administration.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji ordered Ren Huan to take over Chongtao's military and civil duties.

sentences.zh: 魏王通謁李廷安獻蜀樂工二百餘人，有嚴旭者，王衍用為蓬州刺史，帝問曰：「汝何以得刺史？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei's reception officer Li Ting'an presented more than two hundred Shu musicians; among them was Yan Xu, whom Wang Yan had appointed prefect of Pengzhou. The emperor asked, "How did you obtain the prefecture?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei's reception officer Li Ting'an presented more than two hundred Shu musicians. Among them was Yan Xu, whom Wang Yan had made prefect of Pengzhou. The emperor asked, "How did you become prefect?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「以歌。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Through song."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Through singing."

sentences.zh: 帝使歌而善之，許復故任。

translations.literal: The emperor had him sing and approved; he permitted him to resume his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him sing, was pleased, and allowed him to resume his former post.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，孟知祥至成都。

translations.literal: On wuchen Meng Zhixiang reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Meng Zhixiang reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 時新殺郭崇韜，人情未安，知祥慰撫吏民，犒賜將卒，去留帖然。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao had just been killed and popular feeling was unsettled; Zhixiang comforted officials and people, rewarded the generals and soldiers, and those who stayed or left were all at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao had just been killed and the people were uneasy; Zhixiang reassured officials and commoners, rewarded the troops, and all were calmed whether they stayed or left.

sentences.zh: 閩人破陳本，斬之。

translations.literal: The people of Min defeated Chen Ben and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Min forces defeated Chen Ben and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 契丹主擊女真及勃海，恐唐乘虛襲之，戊寅，遣梅老鞋裡來修好。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler attacked the Jurchen and Bohai and feared that Tang would seize the opportunity to strike; on wuyin he sent Meilao Xieli to seek good relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler attacked the Jurchen and Bohai and feared Tang might strike while he was away; on wuyin he sent Meilao Xieli to seek peace.

sentences.zh: 馬彥珪還洛陽，乃下詔暴郭崇韜之罪，並殺其子廷說、廷讓、廷議，於是朝野駭惋，群議紛然，帝使宦者潛察之。

translations.literal: When Ma Yan'gui returned to Luoyang, an edict was then issued exposing Guo Chongtao's crimes, and his sons Tingshuo, Tingrang, and Tingyi were killed as well; thereupon court and countryside were shocked and grieved, public discussion was in uproar, and the emperor had eunuchs secretly observe it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Yan'gui returned to Luoyang, an edict exposed Guo Chongtao's crimes and his sons Tingshuo, Tingrang, and Tingyi were executed as well. Court and countryside were shocked; opinion ran wild, and the emperor had eunuchs watch in secret.

sentences.zh: 保大節度使睦王存乂，崇韜之婿也；

translations.literal: The Baoda military commissioner Prince of Mu Cunyou was Chongtao's son-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: Baoda military commissioner Prince of Mu Cunyou was Chongtao's son-in-law;

sentences.zh: 宦官欲盡去崇韜之黨，言「存乂對諸將攘臂垂泣，為崇韜稱冤，言辭怨望。」

translations.literal: The eunuchs wished to eliminate entirely Chongtao's faction, saying, "Cunyi before the generals wrung his arms and wept, pleading innocence for Chongtao, his words full of resentment and complaint."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs wanted to purge every ally of Guo Chongtao, saying, "Cunyi had stood before the generals wringing his arms and weeping, pleading Chongtao's innocence in language steeped in resentment and grievance."

sentences.zh: 庚辰，幽存乂於第，尋殺之。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Cunyi was confined in his residence; shortly afterward he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Cunyi was placed under house arrest; before long he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 景進言：「河中人有告變，言李繼麟與郭崇韜謀反；

translations.literal: Jing Jin said, "People from Hezhong have reported a plot, saying Li Jilin and Guo Chongtao plotted rebellion together;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Jin reported, "Men from Hezhong have lodged a charge of treason, claiming that Li Jilin conspired with Guo Chongtao to rebel;

sentences.zh: 崇韜死，又與存乂連謀。」

translations.literal: after Chongtao died, he again plotted together with Cunyi."
translations.idiomatic: after Chongtao's death he continued plotting with Cunyi."

sentences.zh: 宦官因共勸帝速除之，帝乃徙繼麟為義成節度使，是夜，遣蕃漢馬步使朱守殷以兵圍其第，驅繼麟出徽安門外殺之，復其姓名曰朱友謙。

translations.literal: The eunuchs together urged the emperor to eliminate him quickly; the emperor therefore transferred Jilin to be military commissioner of Yicheng. That same night he sent the Tu-and-Han cavalry-and-infantry commissioner Zhu Shouyin with troops to surround Jilin's residence, drove Jilin out beyond the Huian Gate and killed him, and restored his original name to Zhu Youqian.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs jointly pressed the emperor to move against him at once. The emperor transferred Jilin to the post of military commissioner of Yicheng, and that very night dispatched Zhu Shouyin, commissioner of Tu and Han cavalry and infantry, with soldiers to surround his residence, drag him beyond the Huian Gate, and execute him—restoring his original name, Zhu Youqian.

sentences.zh: 友謙二子，令德為武信節度使，令錫為忠武節度使；

translations.literal: Youqian's two sons: Lingde was military commissioner of Wuxin, Lingshi was military commissioner of Zhongwu;
translations.idiomatic: Youqian's two sons held distant commands—Lingde as military commissioner of Wuxin, Lingshi as military commissioner of Zhongwu;

sentences.zh: 詔魏王繼岌誅令德於遂州，鄭州刺史王思同誅令錫於許州，河陽節度使李紹奇誅其家人於河中。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Prince of Wei Ji Ji to execute Lingde at Suizhou, Zhengzhou prefect Wang Sitong to execute Lingshi at Xuzhou, and Heyang military commissioner Li Shaoqi to execute his family members at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts went out ordering Prince of Wei Ji Ji to kill Lingde at Suizhou, Zhengzhou prefect Wang Sitong to kill Lingshi at Xuzhou, and Heyang military commissioner Li Shaoqi to execute the rest of the family at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 紹奇至其家，友謙妻張氏帥家人二百餘口見紹奇曰：「朱氏宗族當死，願無濫及平人。」

translations.literal: When Shaoqi arrived at their home, Youqian's wife Lady Zhang led more than two hundred family members to meet Shaoqi and said, "The Zhu clan deserves death; I pray you do not indiscriminately involve ordinary people."
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoqi reached the household, Youqian's wife Lady Zhang appeared with more than two hundred kin and told him, "The Zhu line deserves death—please do not sweep up innocents in the slaughter."

sentences.zh: 乃別其婢僕百人，以其族百口就刑。

translations.literal: She then separated out a hundred maidservants and attendants, and offered up a hundred members of her clan for execution.
translations.idiomatic: She separated out a hundred servants and attendants, then presented a hundred members of her own clan for execution.

sentences.zh: 張氏又取鐵券以示紹奇曰：「此皇帝去年所賜也，我婦人，不識書，不知其何等語也。」

translations.literal: Lady Zhang also took out an iron certificate to show Shaoqi and said, "This was bestowed by the emperor last year. I am a woman and cannot read—I do not know what words it bears."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang then produced an iron certificate of mercy and showed it to Shaoqi. "The emperor gave us this last year," she said. "I am a woman and cannot read—I have no idea what it says."

sentences.zh: 紹奇亦為之慚。

translations.literal: Shaoqi was shamed by this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Even Shaoqi was shamed.

sentences.zh: 友謙舊將吏武等七人，時為刺史，皆坐族誅。

translations.literal: Seven former officers and officials of Youqian including Wu, who were then serving as prefects, were all put to death along with their entire clans.
translations.idiomatic: Seven of Youqian's former commanders and officials, including Wu, who were then serving as prefects, were all executed together with their entire families.

sentences.zh: 時洛中諸軍饑窘，妄為謠言，伶官采之以聞於帝，故郭崇韜、朱友謙皆及於禍。

translations.literal: At that time the various armies in Luoyang were hungry and destitute; false rumors spread at will, and actor-officials collected them and reported them to the emperor—hence both Guo Chongtao and Zhu Youqian met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The armies in Luoyang were starving and desperate; wild rumors flew, and the actor-officials gathered them up and fed them to the emperor—thus both Guo Chongtao and Zhu Youqian were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使兼中書令李嗣源亦為謠言所屬，帝遣朱守殷察之；

translations.literal: Li Siyuan, military commissioner of Chengde and concurrent Grand Counselor, was also implicated by the rumors; the emperor sent Zhu Shouyin to investigate him;
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan, military commissioner of Chengde and concurrent Grand Counselor, was also named in the rumors, and the emperor sent Zhu Shouyin to look into him;

sentences.zh: 守殷私謂嗣源曰：「令公勳業振主，宜自圖歸籓以遠禍。」

translations.literal: Shouyin privately told Siyuan, "Your Lordship's achievements shake the throne; you should consider returning to your fief to distance yourself from calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin took Siyuan aside and said, "Your achievements overshadow the throne. You ought to find a way back to your own domain and keep clear of what is coming."

sentences.zh: 嗣源曰：「吾心不負天地，禍福之來，無所可避，皆委之於命耳。」

translations.literal: Siyuan said, "My heart owes nothing to heaven and earth. When fortune or disaster comes, there is nothing to flee—I leave it all to fate."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan replied, "My conscience is clear before heaven and earth. When fortune or ruin arrives, there is nowhere to run—I can only leave it to fate."

sentences.zh: 時伶宦用事，勳舊人不自保，嗣源危殆者數四，賴宣徽使李紹宏左右營護，以是得全。

translations.literal: At that time actor-eunuchs held power; meritorious old officials could not protect themselves. Siyuan was brought to the brink of danger several times, but thanks to the Palace Directorate commissioner Li Shaohong looking out for him on both sides, he survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: Actor-eunuchs ruled the court; men of old merit could not keep themselves safe. Siyuan was brought to the edge of ruin more than once, and only Li Shaohong of the Palace Directorate, working behind the scenes, saw him through.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌留馬步都指揮使陳留李仁罕、馬軍都指揮使東光潘仁嗣、左廂都指揮使趙廷隱、右廂都指揮使浚儀張業、牙內指揮使文水武漳、驍銳指揮使平恩李廷厚戍成都。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei Ji Ji left Chenliu native Li Renhan as commander of cavalry and infantry, Dongguang native Pan Rensi as commander of the horse army, Zhao Tingyin as commander of the left wing, Junyi native Zhang Ye as commander of the right wing, Wenshui native Wu Zhang as commander of the inner guard, and Ping'en native Li Tinghou as commander of the elite vanguard to garrison Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Ji Ji left Li Renhan of Chenliu in command of cavalry and infantry, Pan Rensi of Dongguang in command of the horse corps, Zhao Tingyin over the left wing, Zhang Ye of Junyi over the right wing, Wu Zhang of Wenshui over the inner guard, and Li Tinghou of Ping'en over the crack troops, all to hold Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 甲申，繼岌發成都，命李紹琛帥萬二千人為後軍，行止常差中軍一捨。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Ji Ji departed from Chengdu and ordered Li Shaochen to lead twelve thousand men as the rear guard, their marches and halts always keeping one stage's distance from the main force.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Ji Ji marched out of Chengdu, putting Li Shaochen in charge of twelve thousand men as rear guard, always keeping one day's march between his column and the main army.

sentences.zh: 二月，己丑朔，以宣徽南院使李紹宏為樞密使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day jichou, Li Shaohong, commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Directorate, was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of jichou, Li Shaohong of the southern bureau of the Palace Directorate was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏博指揮使楊仁晸，將所部兵戍瓦橋，逾年代歸，至貝州，以鄴都空虛，恐兵至為變，敕留屯貝州。

translations.literal: Yang Renjing, commander of Weibo, leading his troops to garrison Waqiao, passed the year of his rotation and was due to return; when he reached Beizhou, because the capital at Ye was empty and there was fear that troops arriving might cause trouble, an order was issued to keep them stationed at Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Renjing, a Weibo commander, had led his men to garrison Waqiao; his tour of duty ran over a year, and when he finally marched home and reached Beizhou, the court—fearing that an empty Ye capital might spark trouble if his column entered—ordered him to remain encamped at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 時天下莫知郭崇韜之罪，民間訛言云：「崇韜殺繼岌，自王於蜀，故族其家。」

translations.literal: At that time no one in the realm knew Guo Chongtao's crime; a false rumor among the people said, "Chongtao killed Ji Ji and made himself king in Shu, and therefore his whole clan was exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: No one in the empire knew what crime Guo Chongtao had committed. Among the people a rumor spread: "Chongtao murdered Ji Ji and crowned himself king in Shu—that is why his entire clan was wiped out."

sentences.zh: 朱友謙子建徽為澶州刺史，帝密敕鄴都監軍史彥瓊殺之。

translations.literal: Zhu Youqian's son Jianhui was prefect of Cao; the emperor secretly ordered the Ye capital military supervisor Shi Yanqiong to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youqian's son Jianhui was prefect of Cao; the emperor secretly ordered Shi Yanqiong, military supervisor at the Ye capital, to kill him.

sentences.zh: 門者白留守王正言曰：「史武德夜半馳馬出城，不言何往。」

translations.literal: The gatekeeper reported to the acting prefect Wang Zhengyan, "Shi Wude galloped out of the city at midnight without saying where he was going."
translations.idiomatic: A gatekeeper told the acting prefect Wang Zhengyan, "Shi Wude rode out of the city at midnight and would not say where he was bound."

sentences.zh: 又訛言云：「皇后以繼岌之死歸咎於帝，已弒帝矣，故急召彥瓊計事。」

translations.literal: Another false rumor said, "The empress blamed the emperor for Ji Ji's death and has already assassinated him, and therefore Yanqiong has been urgently summoned to consult on affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Another rumor ran: "The empress blamed the emperor for Ji Ji's death, has already killed him, and has urgently summoned Yanqiong to plan what comes next."

sentences.zh: 人情愈駭。

translations.literal: Public sentiment grew ever more terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Fear spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 楊仁晸部兵皇甫暉與其徒夜博不勝，因人情不安，遂作亂，劫仁晸曰：「主上所以有天下者，吾魏軍力也；

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui, a soldier under Yang Renjing, and his companions lost at gambling by night; taking advantage of the unsettled mood, they raised a mutiny and seized Renjing, saying, "The reason our lord has the realm is the strength of us Wei troops;
