translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui, a soldier in Yang Renjing's command, lost at dice one night with his comrades; sensing the unrest around them, they mutinied, seized Renjing, and declared, "Our lord holds the realm only because of us Wei soldiers;

sentences.zh: 魏軍甲不去體，馬不解鞍者十餘年，今天下已定，天子不念舊勞，更加猜忌。

translations.literal: Wei troops have not removed their armor from their bodies or unbridled their horses for more than ten years; now that the realm is settled, the Son of Heaven does not remember old service but instead grows ever more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: We Wei men have worn armor and slept in our saddles for more than ten years. Now the realm is settled, yet the emperor forgets our old service and trusts us less every day.

sentences.zh: 遠戍逾年，方喜代歸，去家咫尺，不使相見。

translations.literal: Garrisoned far away for more than a year, we were just rejoicing at rotation and return, yet though home is within a stone's throw, we are not allowed to see our families.
translations.idiomatic: We were posted far off for more than a year, finally due to rotate home—and now, with our families within reach, we are forbidden even to see them.

sentences.zh: 今聞皇后弒逆，京師已亂，將士願與公俱歸，仍表聞朝廷。

translations.literal: Now we hear the empress has committed regicide and the capital is already in chaos; the officers and soldiers wish to return together with you and still report this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: We hear the empress has murdered the emperor and the capital is in turmoil. The men want to march home with you and still send word to the court.

sentences.zh: 若天子萬福，興兵致討，以吾魏博兵力足以拒之，安知不更為富貴之資乎？」

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven enjoys boundless fortune and raises troops to punish us, with our Weibo military strength we can hold them off—who knows but that this may not become a new source of wealth and rank?"
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor lives and sends armies against us, Weibo's strength is enough to hold them off—and who knows? This may yet become our path to fortune."

sentences.zh: 仁晸不從，暉殺之；

translations.literal: Renjing would not agree; Hui killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Renjing refused. Hui killed him;

sentences.zh: 又劫小校，不從，又殺之。

translations.literal: they then seized a junior officer; when he would not agree, they killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: then they seized a junior officer; when he too refused, they killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 效節指揮使趙在禮聞亂，衣不及帶，逾垣而走，暉追及，曳其足而下之，示以二首，在禮懼而從之。

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili, commander of the Xiaojie guard, heard of the mutiny; before he could belt his robe he climbed over the wall and fled. Hui caught up with him, dragged him down by the foot, showed him the two severed heads, and Zaili, in fear, submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili, commander of the Xiaojie guard, heard the uproar and fled over the wall before he could even belt his robe. Hui caught him, pulled him down by the leg, showed him the two severed heads, and Zaili, terrified, went along.

sentences.zh: 亂兵遂奉以為帥，焚掠貝州。

translations.literal: The mutineers then made him their leader and burned and plundered Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers made him their leader and burned and looted Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 暉，魏州人；

translations.literal: Hui was a native of Weizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Hui was from Weizhou;

sentences.zh: 在禮，涿州人也。

translations.literal: Zaili was a native of Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili was from Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，暉等擁在禮南趣臨清、永濟、館陶，所過剽掠。

translations.literal: At dawn, Hui and the others, surrounding Zaili, pressed south toward Linqing, Yongji, and Guantao, plundering everywhere they passed.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Hui and his men, with Zaili at their head, marched south through Linqing, Yongji, and Guantao, looting every place they touched.

sentences.zh: 壬辰晚，有自貝州來告軍亂將犯鄴都者，都巡檢使孫鐸等亟詣史彥瓊，請授甲乘城為備。

translations.literal: Late on renchen, someone arriving from Beizhou reported that the mutinous army would attack the Ye capital; the capital patrol commissioner Sun Duo and others hurried to Shi Yanqiong and requested armor to man the walls in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Late on renchen, a messenger from Beizhou warned that the mutineers were heading for the Ye capital. Sun Duo, chief patrol commissioner, and others rushed to Shi Yanqiong and begged for arms so they could man the walls.

sentences.zh: 彥瓊疑鐸等有異志，曰：「告者雲今日賊至臨清，計程須六日晚方至，為備未晚。」

translations.literal: Yanqiong suspected Duo and the others of ulterior motives and said, "The informant says the rebels reached Linqing today; by reckoning the distance they will not arrive until the evening of the sixth day—it is not too late to prepare."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiong suspected Duo and his men of hidden designs. "The report says the rebels reached Linqing today," he said. "By the usual march they will not arrive until the evening of the sixth day. There is time enough to prepare."

sentences.zh: 孫鐸曰：「賊既作亂，必乘吾未備，晝夜倍道，安肯計程而行！

translations.literal: Sun Duo said, "Once rebels have risen, they are sure to take advantage of our unreadiness and march day and night at double speed—how would they travel by measured stages!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Duo replied, "Rebels never keep to a schedule—they will press day and night while we are still unprepared!

sentences.zh: 請僕射帥眾乘城，鐸募勁兵千人伏於王莽河逆擊之，賊既勢挫，必當離散，然後可撲討也。

translations.literal: I beg the Vice Director to lead the men onto the walls; Duo will recruit a thousand crack troops to lie in ambush at the Wangmang River and strike them head-on. Once the rebels' momentum is broken they will surely scatter, and then they can be hunted down.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Vice Director lead the garrison onto the walls. I will raise a thousand picked men and lie in wait at the Wangmang River to hit them before they reach the city. Break their momentum and they will scatter—then we can mop them up.

sentences.zh: 必俟其至城下，萬一有奸人為內應，則事危矣。」

translations.literal: If we must wait until they reach the foot of the walls, should any traitor within serve as their ally, the affair will become perilous."
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until they are at the gates and some traitor opens the city from within, everything will be lost."

sentences.zh: 彥瓊曰：「但嚴兵守城，何必逆戰！」

translations.literal: Yanqiong said, "Simply keep strict guard on the walls—why must we fight them in the field!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiong said, "Hold the walls with a strong garrison. Why go out to meet them?"

sentences.zh: 是夜，賊前鋒攻北門，弓弩亂髮。

translations.literal: That night the rebel vanguard attacked the north gate; bows and crossbows fired in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rebel vanguard struck the north gate; arrows and bolts flew in every direction.

sentences.zh: 時彥瓊將部兵宿北門樓，聞賊呼聲，即時掠潰。

translations.literal: At the time Yanqiong was lodging with his troops on the north gate tower; hearing the rebels' shouts, they immediately broke and fled in a rout.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiong was billeted with his men on the north gate tower. At the rebels' battle cry his troops broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 彥瓊單騎奔洛陽。

translations.literal: Yanqiong fled alone on horseback to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiong galloped alone to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，賊入鄴都，孫鐸等拒戰不勝，亡去。

translations.literal: On guisi, the rebels entered the Ye capital; Sun Duo and the others resisted but could not prevail and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the rebels entered the Ye capital. Sun Duo and his men fought but could not hold; they fled.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮據宮城，署皇甫暉及軍校趙進為馬步都指揮使，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili seized the palace city, appointed Huangfu Hui and the army officer Zhao Jin as commanders of cavalry and infantry, and let the troops plunder on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili took the palace compound, named Huangfu Hui and the army officer Zhao Jin joint commanders of cavalry and infantry, and unleashed his men on a general looting.

sentences.zh: 進，定州人也。

translations.literal: Jin was a native of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was from Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王正言方據按召吏草奏，無至者，正言怒，其家人曰：「賊已入城，殺掠於市，吏皆逃散，公尚誰呼！」

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan was just seated at his desk summoning clerks to draft a memorial; none came. Zhengyan grew angry, and his household said, "The rebels have already entered the city and are killing and plundering in the markets; the clerks have all fled—whom do you think you are calling!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan sat at his desk calling for clerks to draft a memorial, but no one came. He grew angry. His household said, "The rebels are already in the city, killing and looting in the streets—the clerks have all run. Who do you think will answer?"

sentences.zh: 正言驚曰：「吾初不知也。」

translations.literal: Zhengyan said in alarm, "I did not know this at first."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan started. "I had no idea."

sentences.zh: 又索馬，不能得，乃帥僚佐步出門謁在禮，再拜請罪。

translations.literal: He then sought a horse but could not obtain one, and so led his staff on foot out the gate to pay court to Zaili, bowing twice to plead guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a horse and could not get one, so he walked out with his staff to call on Zaili and bowed twice to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 在禮亦拜，曰：「士座思歸耳，尚書重德，勿自卑屈。」

translations.literal: Zaili also bowed and said, "The soldiers only long to return home; Minister, your virtue is weighty—do not demean yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Zaili bowed in return. "The men only wanted to go home," he said. "Minister, you are a man of standing—do not abase yourself."

sentences.zh: 慰諭遣之。

translations.literal: He comforted and reassured him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted him and let him go.

sentences.zh: 眾推在禮為魏博留後，具奏其狀。

translations.literal: The multitude pushed Zaili to be acting military commissioner of Weibo and submitted a full report of the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The troops proclaimed Zaili acting military commissioner of Weibo and sent a full report to the court.

sentences.zh: 北京留守張憲家在鄴都，在禮厚撫之，遣使以書誘憲，憲不發封，斬其使以聞。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian, acting prefect of the northern capital, had his family home in the Ye capital; Zaili treated them generously and sent an envoy with a letter to entice Xian. Xian did not break the seal, beheaded the envoy, and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, acting prefect of the northern capital, had family in Ye. Zaili treated them well and sent a messenger with a letter to win him over. Xian never broke the seal; he beheaded the messenger and reported what had happened.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以景進為銀青光祿大夫、檢校右散騎常侍兼御吏大夫、上柱國。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Jing Jin was appointed Silver-Gleam Grandee of Splendid Happiness, acting Right Regular Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Jing Jin was made Silver-Gleam Grandee of Splendid Happiness, acting Right Regular Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with the rank Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 丙申，史彥瓊至洛陽。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Shi Yanqiong reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Shi Yanqiong arrived in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝問可為大將者於樞密使李紹宏，紹宏復請用李紹欽，帝許之，令條上方略。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Li Shaohong who could serve as a great general; Shaohong again recommended Li Shaoqin, the emperor agreed, and ordered him to submit a written plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Li Shaohong, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, whom to appoint as field commander. Shaohong again recommended Li Shaoqin. The emperor agreed and told him to submit a plan of campaign.

sentences.zh: 紹欽所請偏裨，皆梁舊將，己所善者，帝疑之而止。

translations.literal: The subordinate commanders Shaoqin requested were all old Liang generals whom he favored; the emperor grew suspicious and halted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The subordinate commanders Shaoqin asked for were all old Liang officers he favored personally. The emperor grew suspicious and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 皇后曰：「此小事，不足煩大將，紹榮可辦也。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "This is a small affair, not worth troubling a great general—Shaorong can handle it."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "This is a small matter—not worth a full field commander. Shaorong can manage it."

sentences.zh: 帝乃命歸德節度使李紹榮將騎三千詣鄴都招撫，亦征諸道兵，備其不服。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Guidde military commissioner Li Shaorong to lead three thousand horsemen to the Ye capital to offer reassurance and enlistment, and also summoned troops from the various circuits in case they would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Li Shaorong, military commissioner of Guidde, to take three thousand cavalry to Ye to offer terms, while also calling up troops from the circuits in case the rebels refused.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜之死也，李紹琛謂董璋曰：「公復欲呫囁誰門乎？」

translations.literal: At the time of Guo Chongtao's death, Li Shaochen said to Dong Zhang, "Do you wish again to fawn and whisper at whose gate?"
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Chongtao was killed, Li Shaochen said to Dong Zhang, "Whose door do you plan to crawl back to now?"

sentences.zh: 璋懼，謝罪。

translations.literal: Zhang, in fear, apologized for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, frightened, apologized.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌軍還至武連，遇敕使，諭以朱友謙已伏誅，令董璋將兵之遂州誅朱令德。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wei's army returned as far as Wulian, they met an imperial messenger who announced that Zhu Youqian had already been executed and ordered Dong Zhang to lead troops to Suizhou to execute Zhu Lingde.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei's army had marched back as far as Wulian when an imperial messenger arrived with word that Zhu Youqian had been executed and orders for Dong Zhang to take troops to Suizhou and kill Zhu Lingde.

sentences.zh: 時紹琛將後軍魏城，聞之，以帝不委己殺令德而委璋，大驚。

translations.literal: At the time Shaochen was leading the rear guard at Weicheng; hearing this, he was greatly alarmed that the emperor had not entrusted him with killing Lingde but had entrusted Zhang instead.
translations.idiomatic: Shaochen was then leading the rear guard at Weicheng. Learning that the emperor had entrusted Lingde's death to Zhang rather than to him, he was deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 俄而璋過紹琛軍，不謁。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Zhang passed Shaochen's army but did not pay a visit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang passed Shaochen's camp without calling on him.

sentences.zh: 紹琛怒，乘酒謂諸將曰：「國家南取大梁，西定巴、蜀，皆郭公之謀而吾之戰功也；

translations.literal: Shaochen, angry and taking advantage of wine, told the generals, "The state's conquest of Daliang in the south and pacification of Ba and Shu in the west were all Lord Guo's plans and my battlefield achievements;
translations.idiomatic: Drunk and furious, Shaochen told his officers, "The realm's conquest of Daliang in the south and pacification of Ba and Shu in the west rested on Lord Guo's strategy and my victories in the field;

sentences.zh: 至於去逆效順，與國家掎角以破梁，則朱公也。

translations.literal: as for casting off rebellion and submitting in loyalty, joining the state in pincer action to break Liang—that was Lord Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: and when it came to turning against the rebels and standing with the throne to break Liang—that was Lord Zhu.

sentences.zh: 今朱、郭皆無罪族滅，歸朝之後，行及我矣。

translations.literal: Now Zhu and Guo, though guiltless, have had their clans exterminated; after we return to court, the same will reach me.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhu and Guo, though innocent, have been wiped out to the last kin. Once we reach the capital, my turn will come.

sentences.zh: 冤哉，天乎！

translations.literal: How unjust—O heaven!
translations.idiomatic: What injustice—heaven help us!

sentences.zh: 奈何！」

translations.literal: What is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 紹琛所將多河中兵，河中將焦武等同號哭於軍門曰：「西平王何罪，闔門屠膾！

translations.literal: Most of those Shaochen led were Hezhong troops; the Hezhong commander Jiao Wu and others wailed together at the army gate, saying, "What crime did the Prince of Xiping commit, that his whole household was butchered!
translations.idiomatic: Most of Shaochen's men were from Hezhong. Jiao Wu and other Hezhong officers wailed at the camp gate: "What crime did the Prince of Xiping commit, that his entire house was slaughtered!

sentences.zh: 我屬歸則與史武等同誅，決不復東矣。」

translations.literal: If we of this company return, we will be executed together with Shi Wu and the rest—we will never go east again."
translations.idiomatic: If we march home we will die like Shi Wu and the rest—we will never go east again."

sentences.zh: 是日，魏王繼岌至泥溪，紹琛至劍州遣人白繼岌云：「河中將士號哭不止，欲為亂。」

translations.literal: That day the Prince of Wei reached Nixi; Shaochen reached Jianzhou and sent someone to inform Ji Ji, saying, "The Hezhong officers and soldiers wail without cease and wish to raise a mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: That day Prince of Wei reached Nixi. Shaochen reached Jianzhou and sent word to Ji Ji: "The Hezhong men will not stop wailing—they mean to mutiny."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，紹琛自劍州擁兵西還，自稱西川節度、三川制置等使，移檄成都，稱奉詔代孟知祥，招諭蜀人，三日間眾至五萬。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Shaochen from Jianzhou led his troops back west, styled himself military commissioner of Xichuan and commissioner for the administration of the Three Rivers, issued a proclamation to Chengdu claiming he acted on imperial orders to replace Meng Zhixiang, and summoned the people of Shu; within three days his force reached fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Shaochen marched west from Jianzhou at the head of his army, declared himself military commissioner of Xichuan and commissioner for the administration of the Three Rivers, and sent a proclamation to Chengdu claiming imperial orders to replace Meng Zhixiang. Within three days fifty thousand men rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，李繼曮至鳳翔，監軍使柴重厚不以符印與之，促令詣闕。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Li Jiyao reached Fengxiang; the military supervisor Chai Zhonghou would not give him the seals and credentials and urged him to proceed to the court.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Li Jiyao reached Fengxiang. Military supervisor Chai Zhonghou refused to hand over the seals and credentials and pressed him to continue to the capital.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏王繼岌至利州，李紹琛遣人斷桔柏津。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Prince of Wei reached Lizhou; Li Shaochen sent men to cut the Jiebai crossing.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Prince of Wei reached Lizhou. Shaochen sent men to destroy the Jiebai crossing.

sentences.zh: 繼岌聞之，以任圜為副招討使，將步騎七千，與都指揮使梁漢顒、監軍李延安追討之。

translations.literal: Ji Ji, hearing this, appointed Ren Yuan as deputy pacification commissioner and sent seven thousand infantry and cavalry together with the commander-in-chief Liang Hanyong and the military supervisor Li Yan'an in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Ji Ji made Ren Yuan deputy pacification commissioner and sent seven thousand foot and horse soldiers under commander-in-chief Liang Hanyong and military supervisor Li Yan'an in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 庚子，邢州左右步直兵趙太等四百人據城自稱安國留後；

translations.literal: On gengzi, four hundred infantry guards of Xingzhou including Zhao Tai seized the city and styled themselves acting military commissioners of Anguo;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, four hundred infantry guards at Xingzhou, led by Zhao Tai, seized the city and declared themselves acting military commissioners of Anguo;

sentences.zh: 詔東北面招討副使李紹真討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the deputy pacification commissioner of the northeast Li Shaozhen to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: an edict ordered Li Shaozhen, deputy pacification commissioner of the northeast, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，任圜先令別將何建崇擊劍門關，下之。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Ren Yuan first ordered the detached commander He Jianchong to attack Jianmen Pass and take it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Ren Yuan first sent detached commander He Jianchong to assault Jianmen Pass and take it.

sentences.zh: 李紹榮至鄴都，攻其南門，遣人以敕招諭之，趙在禮以羊酒犒師，拜於城上曰：「將士思家擅歸，相公誠善為敷奏，得免於死，敢不自新！」

translations.literal: Li Shaorong reached the Ye capital and attacked its south gate; he sent men with an imperial edict to offer reassurance. Zhao Zaili rewarded the army with sheep and wine and bowed from atop the wall, saying, "The soldiers, longing for home, returned on their own; if Your Lordship will truly plead our case well so we may escape death, how would we dare not reform ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaorong reached the Ye capital and assaulted the south gate, then sent men with an imperial edict offering terms. Zhao Zaili sent out sheep and wine to reward the troops and bowed from the wall: "The men came home on their own because they missed their families. If you will truly plead our case so we may live, we dare not fail to mend our ways!"

sentences.zh: 遂以敕遍諭軍士。

translations.literal: He then had the edict read throughout to all the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He had the edict read aloud to every soldier.

sentences.zh: 史彥瓊戟手大罵曰：「群死賊，城破萬段！」

translations.literal: Shi Yanqiong, halberd in hand, cursed loudly, "Pack of dead rebels—when the city falls you shall be torn into ten thousand pieces!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanqiong, halberd in hand, shouted curses: "Pack of dead rebels—when this wall falls you will be torn limb from limb!"

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉胃其眾曰：「觀史武德之言，上不赦我矣。」

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui addressed his troops and said, "Judging by Shi Wude's words, the emperor will not pardon us."
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui told his men: "Listen to Shi Wude—the emperor will never spare us."

sentences.zh: 因聚噪，掠敕書，手壞之，守陴拒戰，紹榮攻之不利，以狀聞，帝怒曰：「克城之日，勿遣□類！」

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered in uproar, snatched the edict, tore it apart by hand, manned the battlements and resisted; Shaorong's attack did not succeed. When he reported the situation, the emperor said in anger, "On the day the city is taken, leave none alive!"
translations.idiomatic: The men roared, seized the edict, tore it to pieces, manned the walls, and fought back. Shaorong's assault failed. When he reported what had happened, the emperor raged: "When the city falls, leave none alive!"

sentences.zh: 大發諸軍討之。

translations.literal: He mobilized armies on a great scale to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized armies from every quarter to crush them.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，紹榮退屯澶州。

translations.literal: On renyin, Shaorong withdrew and encamped at Cao.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Shaorong pulled back and encamped at Cao.

sentences.zh: 甲辰夜，從馬直軍士王溫等五人殺軍使，謀作亂，擒斬之。

translations.literal: On the night of jiachen, five soldiers of the Personal Cavalry Guard including Wang Wen killed the army commissioner and plotted a mutiny; they were seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jiachen, five soldiers of the Personal Cavalry Guard, led by Wang Wen, murdered their army commissioner and plotted mutiny. They were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 從馬直指揮使郭從謙，本優人也，優名郭門高。

translations.literal: The Personal Cavalry Guard commander Guo Congqian was originally an actor; his stage name was Guo Mengao.
translations.idiomatic: The commander of the Personal Cavalry Guard, Guo Congqian, had begun as an actor; on stage he was known as Guo Mengao.

sentences.zh: 帝與梁相拒於得勝，募勇士挑戰，從謙應募，俘斬而還，由是益有寵。

translations.literal: When the emperor faced Liang in stalemate at Desheng, he recruited brave men to challenge the enemy; Congqian answered the call, returned with captives and severed heads, and from this gained ever greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor faced Liang in stalemate at Desheng, he called for volunteers to challenge the enemy. Congqian stepped forward, returned with prisoners and severed heads, and from that day won ever greater favor.

sentences.zh: 帝選諸軍驍勇者為親軍，分置四指揮，號從馬直，從謙自軍使積功至指揮使。

translations.literal: The emperor selected the boldest fighters from the various armies to form his personal guard, divided them into four commands called the Personal Cavalry Guard, and Congqian rose from army commissioner through accumulated merit to commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor picked the fiercest men from every army for his personal guard, organized them into four commands called the Personal Cavalry Guard, and Congqian rose from army commissioner through repeated merit to full commander.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜方用事，從謙以叔父事之，睦王存乂以從謙為假子。

translations.literal: When Guo Chongtao was in power, Congqian treated him as an uncle; Prince of Mu Cunyi took Congqian as a foster son.
translations.idiomatic: While Guo Chongtao held power, Congqian treated him as an uncle might be treated; Prince of Mu Cunyi took Congqian as a foster son.

sentences.zh: 及崇韜、存乂得罪，從謙數以私財饗從馬直諸校，對之流涕，言崇韜之冤。

translations.literal: When Chongtao and Cunyi met with punishment, Congqian repeatedly used his private wealth to feast the various officers of the Personal Cavalry Guard, weeping before them and speaking of Chongtao's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongtao and Cunyi fell, Congqian repeatedly spent his own money to feast the officers of the Personal Cavalry Guard, weeping before them and insisting on Chongtao's innocence.

sentences.zh: 及王溫作亂，帝戲之曰：「汝既負我附崇韜、存乂，又教王溫反，欲何為也？」

translations.literal: When Wang Wen raised a mutiny, the emperor jested with him, saying, "You have already betrayed me to attach yourself to Chongtao and Cunyi, and now you have taught Wang Wen to rebel—what do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wen mutinied, the emperor teased him: "You turned against me for Chongtao and Cunyi, and now you put Wang Wen up to rebellion—what are you after?"

sentences.zh: 從謙益懼。

translations.literal: Congqian grew all the more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Congqian grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 既退，陰謂諸校曰：「主上以王溫之故，俟鄴都平定，盡坑若曹。

translations.literal: After he withdrew, he secretly told the various officers, "Because of Wang Wen, once the Ye capital is pacified the emperor will bury you all alive.
translations.idiomatic: After he withdrew, he told the officers in secret: "Because of Wang Wen, once Ye is pacified the emperor means to bury every one of you alive.

sentences.zh: 家之所有宜盡市酒肉，勿為久計也。」

translations.literal: Whatever your households possess, you should spend it all buying wine and meat—do not plan for the long term."
translations.idiomatic: Spend everything you own on wine and meat while you can—do not plan for tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 由是親軍皆不自安。

translations.literal: From this, all of the personal guard grew restless in mind.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward, the emperor's personal guard lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，王衍至長安，有詔止之。

translations.literal: On yisi, Wang Yan reached Chang'an; an edict ordered him to halt.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Wang Yan arrived at Chang'an and was commanded by edict to stop.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝諸弟雖領節度使，皆留京師，但食其俸。

translations.literal: Earlier, though the emperor's younger brothers held posts as military commissioners, they all remained in the capital and merely received their salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the emperor's younger brothers held military commissioner titles, yet they all stayed in the capital on salary alone.

sentences.zh: 戊申，始命護國節度使永王存霸至河中。

translations.literal: On wushen, the emperor first ordered Prince Yong Cunba, military commissioner of Huguo, to proceed to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, he first dispatched Prince Yong Cunba, Huguo military commissioner, to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 丁未，李紹榮以諸道兵再攻鄴都。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Li Shaorong again attacked the Ye capital with troops from the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Li Shaorong led armies from every circuit in another assault on the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，裨將楊重霸帥眾數百登城，後無繼者，重霸等皆死。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the deputy general Yang Zhongba led several hundred men up onto the walls; with no one following after them, Zhongba and the rest all died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Deputy General Yang Zhongba scaled the walls at the head of several hundred men, but no reinforcements came, and Zhongba and all who followed him were killed.

sentences.zh: 賊知不赦，堅守無降意。

translations.literal: The rebels knew they would not be pardoned and held firm with no thought of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that mercy was denied them, the rebels dug in and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 朝廷患之，日發中使促魏王繼岌東還。

translations.literal: The court was troubled by this and every day dispatched palace envoys to urge Prince of Wei Jiji to return east.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew alarmed and sent palace envoys day after day, pressing Prince of Wei Jiji to turn back east.

sentences.zh: 繼岌以中軍精兵皆從任圜討李紹琛，留利州待之，未得還。

translations.literal: Jiji had sent his central army's elite troops with Ren Huan to suppress Li Shaochen, and remained at Lizhou awaiting them—he could not yet return.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji had committed his best central troops to Ren Huan's campaign against Li Shaochen and was waiting at Lizhou; he could not yet come back.

sentences.zh: 李紹榮討趙在禮久無功，趙太據邢州未下。

translations.literal: Li Shaorong's campaign against Zhao Zaili had long yielded no success, and Zhao Tai still held Xingzhou without being taken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaorong had gained nothing after a long pursuit of Zhao Zaili, and Zhao Tai still held Xingzhou unconquered.

sentences.zh: 滄州軍亂，小校王景戡討定之，因自為留後；

translations.literal: The army at Cangzhou mutinied; a junior officer, Wang Jingkan, quelled the disturbance and then made himself acting governor;
translations.idiomatic: Troops at Cangzhou mutinied, and a junior officer named Wang Jingkan crushed the revolt and proclaimed himself acting governor;

sentences.zh: 河朔州縣告亂者相繼。

translations.literal: Counties and prefectures north of the Yellow River reported rebellion one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of uprising poured in from prefectures and counties across Hebei.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自征鄴都，宰相、樞密使皆言京師根本，車駕不可輕動，帝曰：「諸將無可使者。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to campaign in person against the Ye capital; the chief ministers and the Bureau of Military Affairs all said that the capital was the root foundation and that the imperial carriage must not be lightly moved. The emperor said, "Among the generals there is none fit for the task."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to lead the campaign against Ye in person, but the chief ministers and the Bureau of Military Affairs argued that the capital was the foundation of the realm and that the throne must not stir lightly. The emperor said, "There is no general I can send."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「李嗣源最為勳舊。」

translations.literal: They all said, "Li Siyuan is foremost among the meritorious veterans."
translations.idiomatic: They replied as one, "Li Siyuan stands first among the old heroes of the founding."

sentences.zh: 帝心忌嗣源，曰：「吾惜嗣源，欲留宿衛。」

translations.literal: The emperor, jealous of Siyuan at heart, said, "I value Siyuan and wish to keep him for palace guard duty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who secretly feared Siyuan, said, "I hold Siyuan dear and would keep him at my side as palace guard."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「他人無可者。」

translations.literal: They all said, "There is no one else suitable."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "There is no one else who will serve."

sentences.zh: 忠武節度使張全義亦言：「河朔多事，久則患深，宜令總管進討；

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Zhongwu Zhang Quanyi also said, "Hebei is beset with troubles; if this goes on the harm will deepen—the overall commander should be ordered to advance and suppress them;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi, military commissioner of Zhongwu, added, "Hebei is in turmoil; delay will only deepen the wound. The overall commander should be sent to strike at once;

sentences.zh: 若倚紹榮輩，未見成功之期。」

translations.literal: If one relies on men like Shaorong, no day of success is in sight."
translations.idiomatic: If we rely on men like Shaorong, victory remains far off."

sentences.zh: 李紹宏亦屢言之，帝以內外所薦，久乃許之，甲寅，命嗣源將親軍討鄴都。

translations.literal: Li Shaohong also said so repeatedly; as both court and provinces recommended him, the emperor long delayed but finally consented. On jiayin he ordered Siyuan to lead the personal guard against the Ye capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaohong urged the same again and again. Pressed by recommendations from within and without, the emperor at last agreed. On jiayin he ordered Siyuan to lead the personal guard against the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 延州言綏、銀軍亂，剽州城。

translations.literal: Yanzhou reported that the armies of Sui and Yin had mutinied and plundered the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Word came from Yanzhou that troops in Sui and Yin had mutinied and raided the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 董璋將兵二萬屯綿州，會任圜討李紹琛。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang led twenty thousand troops encamped at Mianzhou, joining Ren Huan to suppress Li Shaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang encamped at Mianzhou with twenty thousand men to join Ren Huan against Li Shaochen.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中使崔延琛至成都，遇紹琛軍，紹之曰：「吾奉詔召孟郎，公若緩兵，自當得蜀。」

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the palace envoy Cui Yanchen to Chengdu; he encountered Shaochen's army. Shaochen said to him, "I carry an edict summoning Lord Meng; if you slow your march, you will naturally secure Shu for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the palace envoy Cui Yanchen to Chengdu. On the road he met Shaochen's army. Shaochen told him, "I bear an edict to summon Lord Meng. Slow your march, and Shu will fall to you of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 既至成都，勸孟知祥為戰守備。

translations.literal: After he reached Chengdu, he urged Meng Zhixiang to prepare for both battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Chengdu, he urged Meng Zhixiang to ready the city for war and siege alike.

sentences.zh: 知祥浚壕樹柵，遣馬步都指揮使李仁罕將四萬人，驍銳指揮使李延厚將二千人討紹琛。

translations.literal: Zhixiang dug moats and raised palisades, then dispatched the cavalry-and-infantry commander Li Renhan with forty thousand men and the elite vanguard commander Li Yanhou with two thousand to attack Shaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang dug moats and raised palisades, then sent Li Renhan, commander of cavalry and infantry, with forty thousand men, and Li Yanhou, commander of the elite vanguard, with two thousand, to crush Shaochen.

sentences.zh: 延厚集其眾詢之曰：「有少壯勇銳，欲立功求富貴者東！

translations.literal: Yanhou assembled his troops and asked them, "Any among you who are young, strong, and bold, seeking merit and fortune—go east!
translations.idiomatic: Yanhou gathered his men and called out, "You who are young, strong, and hungry for glory and reward—step east!

sentences.zh: 衰疾畏懦，厭行陳者西！」

translations.literal: Those who are aged, sick, timid, and weary of battle lines—go west!"
translations.idiomatic: You who are old, sick, timid, and sick of the field—step west!"

sentences.zh: 得選兵七百人以行。

translations.literal: He chose seven hundred men and set out.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred volunteers were chosen, and they marched.

sentences.zh: 是日，任圜軍追及紹琛於漢州，紹琛出兵逆戰；

translations.literal: That same day, Ren Huan's army caught up with Shaochen at Hanzhou, and Shaochen marched out to meet them in battle;
translations.idiomatic: That day Ren Huan's army overtook Shaochen at Hanzhou, and Shaochen led his troops out to give battle;

sentences.zh: 招討掌書記張礪請伏精兵於後，以贏兵誘之，圜從之，使董璋以東川贏兵先戰而卻。

translations.literal: The campaign secretary Zhang Li asked to hide elite troops in the rear and lure the enemy with weak forces; Ren Huan agreed and had Dong Zhang advance first with Shu weaklings, then fall back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li, secretary of the expedition, proposed hiding crack troops in the rear and baiting the enemy with a weak front. Ren Huan agreed and sent Dong Zhang forward with expendable eastern-Shu troops to engage and then retreat.

sentences.zh: 紹琛輕圜書生，又見其兵贏，極力追之，伏兵發，大破之，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Shaochen despised Ren Huan as a mere scholar; seeing his troops were weak, he pursued with all his strength—the ambush sprang, routing him utterly and taking several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shaochen looked down on Ren Huan as a bookish man, saw only a ragged force before him, and gave chase with everything he had. The ambush rose, shattered his army, and left several thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 自是紹琛入漢州，閉城不出。

translations.literal: From then on Shaochen withdrew into Hanzhou and shut the gates, refusing to emerge.
translations.idiomatic: After that Shaochen withdrew into Hanzhou, barred the gates, and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁已朔，李紹真奏克刑州，擒趙太等。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingyi the first day of the month, Li Shaozhen reported the capture of Xingzhou and the seizure of Zhao Tai and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day dingyi, Li Shaozhen reported that Xingzhou had fallen and that Zhao Tai and his fellows had been taken.

sentences.zh: 庚申，紹真引兵至鄴都，營於城西北，以太等徇於鄴都城下而殺之。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Shaozhen led his troops to the Ye capital, encamped northwest of the city, paraded Tai and the rest beneath the walls, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Shaozhen marched to the Ye capital and encamped northwest of the walls. He paraded Tai and the others beneath the city and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以威武節度副使王廷翰為威武節度使。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Deputy Military Commissioner of Weiwu Wang Tinghan was appointed military commissioner of Weiwu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Wang Tinghan, deputy military commissioner of Weiwu, was made full military commissioner of Weiwu.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，李嗣源至鄴都，營於城西南；

translations.literal: On renxu, Li Siyuan reached the Ye capital and encamped southwest of the city;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Li Siyuan arrived at the Ye capital and pitched camp southwest of the walls;

sentences.zh: 甲子，嗣源下令軍中，詰旦攻城。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Siyuan issued orders throughout the army to assault the city at daybreak.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Siyuan ordered the army to storm the city at first light.

sentences.zh: 是夜，從馬直軍士張破敗作亂，帥眾大噪，殺都將，焚營舍。

translations.literal: That night, Zhang Popo, a soldier of the Personal Cavalry Guard, raised a mutiny, led the men in a great clamor, killed the commandant, and burned the camp buildings.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhang Popo, a soldier of the Personal Cavalry Guard, mutinied. He roused the ranks in uproar, killed the commandant, and set the camp ablaze.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，亂兵逼中軍，嗣源帥親軍拒戰，不能敵，亂兵益熾。

translations.literal: At daybreak the mutineers pressed on the central command; Siyuan led the personal guard to resist but could not prevail, and the mutineers grew all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the mutineers closed on headquarters. Siyuan led the personal guard to hold them off but could not, and the rebellion swelled.

sentences.zh: 嗣源叱而問之曰：「爾曹欲何為？」

translations.literal: Siyuan shouted them down and demanded, "What do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan shouted them down and asked, "What is it you want?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「將士從主上十年，百戰以得天下。

translations.literal: They answered, "Your soldiers have followed the sovereign ten years, fighting a hundred battles to win the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We have followed the sovereign ten years, through a hundred battles, to win the realm.

sentences.zh: 今主上棄恩任威，貝州戍卒思歸，主上不赦，云『克城之後，當盡坑魏博之軍』；

translations.literal: Now the sovereign casts aside kindness and trusts only force. The garrison at Beizhou longed to return home, yet the sovereign would not pardon them, saying, 'After the city falls, all the armies of Weibo will be buried alive';
translations.idiomatic: Now the sovereign casts off kindness and rules by terror. The garrison at Beizhou only wanted to go home, yet he would not pardon them, saying, 'When the city falls, every soldier of Weibo will be buried alive';

sentences.zh: 近從馬直數卒喧競，遽欲盡誅其眾。

translations.literal: Recently a few soldiers of the Personal Cavalry Guard raised a quarrel, and he suddenly meant to execute their entire company.
translations.idiomatic: Only lately a handful of Personal Cavalry Guard soldiers quarreled, and he meant at once to slaughter the whole company.

sentences.zh: 我輩初無叛心，但畏死耳。

translations.literal: We had no rebellion in our hearts at first—we were only afraid of death.
translations.idiomatic: We did not set out to rebel; we were only afraid to die.

sentences.zh: 今眾議欲與城中合勢擊退諸道之軍，請主上帝河南，令公帝河北，為軍民之主。」

translations.literal: Now the company wishes to join forces with the city, drive back the armies of the various circuits, and ask the sovereign to reign over Henan while we make you emperor north of the Yellow River, master of soldier and civilian alike."
translations.idiomatic: Now the men wish to join with the city, drive off the armies of every circuit, and ask the sovereign to rule Henan while we make you emperor of Hebei, lord of soldier and civilian alike."

sentences.zh: 嗣源泣諭之，不從。

translations.literal: Siyuan wept as he pleaded with them, but they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan wept as he reasoned with them, but they would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 嗣源曰：「爾不用吾言，任爾所為，我自歸京師。」

translations.literal: Siyuan said, "If you will not heed my words, do as you please—I shall return to the capital myself."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan said, "If you will not listen, do as you will. I shall return to the capital alone."

sentences.zh: 亂兵拔白刃環之，曰：「此輩虎狼也，不識尊卑，令公去欲何之！」

translations.literal: The mutineers drew white blades and surrounded him, crying, "These men are wolves—they know neither high nor low! Where does Your Lordship think you are going!"
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers bared their blades and ringed him about, shouting, "These are wolves who know neither rank nor duty! Where do you think you are going!"

sentences.zh: 因擁嗣源及李紹真等入城，城中不受外兵，皇甫暉逆擊張破敗，斬之，外兵皆潰。

translations.literal: They then forced Siyuan, Li Shaozhen, and the rest into the city. The city would not admit outside troops; Huangfu Hui counterattacked Zhang Popo, beheaded him, and the outside troops all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They then forced Siyuan, Li Shaozhen, and the others into the city. The city would not admit the outside troops. Huangfu Hui turned on Zhang Popo, cut him down, and the outside force broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮帥諸校迎拜嗣源，泣謝曰：「將士輩負令公，敢不惟命是聽！」

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili led the various officers forward to bow in welcome and weeping apologized, "We soldiers have failed Your Lordship—we dare not disobey a single command!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili led the officers forward to bow and welcome Siyuan, weeping as he said, "We have failed you, my lord—we dare not disobey your command!"

sentences.zh: 嗣源詭說在禮曰：「凡舉大事，須藉兵力，今外兵流散無所歸，我為公出收之。」

translations.literal: Siyuan deceived Zaili, saying, "Any great undertaking requires military strength. The outside troops have scattered with nowhere to go—I will go out for you and gather them in."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan spoke craftily to Zaili: "Every great venture needs soldiers. The outside troops have scattered with nowhere to turn. Let me go out for you and bring them in."

sentences.zh: 在禮乃聽嗣源、紹真俱出城，宿魏縣，散兵稍有至者。

translations.literal: Zaili then allowed Siyuan and Shaozhen both to leave the city. They lodged at Wei County, and scattered soldiers gradually began to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili let Siyuan and Shaozhen leave the city together. They lodged at Wei County, and scattered soldiers began to drift in.

sentences.zh: 漢州無城塹，樹木為柵。

translations.literal: Hanzhou had no walls or moat and used timber to build a palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhou had neither wall nor moat and relied on a timber palisade.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，任圜進攻其柵，縱火焚之，李紹琛引兵出戰於金雁橋，兵敗，與十餘騎奔綿竹，追擒之。

translations.literal: On yichou, Ren Huan assaulted the palisade and set it ablaze. Li Shaochen led troops out to fight at the Golden Goose Bridge, was defeated, and fled to Mianzhu with a dozen horsemen—they overtook and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Ren Huan stormed the palisade and burned it. Li Shaochen marched out to fight at the Golden Goose Bridge, was routed, and fled toward Mianzhu with a dozen riders. Pursuers overtook and captured him.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥自至漢州犒軍，與任圜、董璋置酒高會，引李紹琛檻車至座中，知祥自酌大卮飲之，謂曰：「公已擁節旄，又有平蜀之功，何患不富貴，而求入此檻車邪！」

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang went in person to Hanzhou to reward the troops, held a lofty feast with Ren Huan and Dong Zhang, and had Li Shaochen brought in a caged cart to the seats. Zhixiang poured himself a great cup and drank, then said, "You already hold a commissioner's banner and earned merit in pacifying Shu—what lack of wealth and rank could trouble you, that you should seek to enter this caged cart!"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang came in person to Hanzhou to feast the army. He raised cups with Ren Huan and Dong Zhang, had Li Shaochen brought before them in a caged cart, poured himself a great bowl and drank, and said, "You already bear a commissioner's banner and won merit in pacifying Shu. What wealth and rank could you lack, that you should choose this cage!"

sentences.zh: 紹琛曰：「郭侍中佐命功第一，兵不血刃取兩川，一旦無罪族誅；

translations.literal: Shaochen said, "Vice Minister Guo ranked first in the merit of aiding the founding mandate; he took both river provinces without shedding blood—yet one morning, innocent, his entire clan was executed;
translations.idiomatic: Shaochen said, "Vice Minister Guo stood first in the merit of founding the dynasty and took both river provinces without drawing a blade—yet one morning, though guiltless, his whole clan was slaughtered;

sentences.zh: 如紹琛輩安保首領！

translations.literal: How can men like Shaochen keep their heads safe!
translations.idiomatic: How can men like me hope to keep our heads!

sentences.zh: 以此不敢歸朝耳。」

translations.literal: For this reason I dare not return to court."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dare not return to court."

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌既獲紹琛，乃引兵倍道而東。

translations.literal: After Prince of Wei Jiji had captured Shaochen, he led his army east by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince of Wei Jiji had taken Shaochen, he marched east at double speed.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥獲陝虢都指揮使汝陰李肇、河中都指揮使千乘侯弘實，以肇為牙內馬步都指揮使，弘實副之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang captured Li Zhao of Ruyin, commander of Shan-Guo, and Hou Hongshi of Qiancheng, commander of Hezhong, appointing Zhao as commander of palace cavalry and infantry with Hongshi as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang took Li Zhao of Ruyin, commander of Shan-Guo, and Hou Hongshi of Qiancheng, commander of Hezhong, and made Zhao commander of palace cavalry and infantry with Hongshi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 蜀中群盜猶未息，知祥擇廉吏使治州縣，蠲除橫賦，安集流散，下寬大之令，與民更始。

translations.literal: Bandits in Shu had not yet been quelled. Zhixiang chose upright officials to govern the prefectures and counties, remitted illegal levies, settled the displaced, and issued lenient orders, making a fresh start with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry in Shu had not yet subsided. Zhixiang sent honest officials to govern the prefectures and counties, lifted illegal exactions, gathered the displaced, and issued clemency, offering the people a new beginning.

sentences.zh: 遣左廂都指揮使趙廷隱、右廂都指揮使張業將兵分討群盜，悉誅之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Zhao Tingyin, commander of the left wing, and Zhang Ye, commander of the right wing, to lead troops in separate campaigns against the bandits and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhao Tingyin, commander of the left wing, and Zhang Ye, commander of the right wing, to hunt down the bandits in separate columns and put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源之為亂兵所逼也，李紹榮有眾萬人，營於城南，嗣源遣牙將張虔釗、高行周等七人相繼召之，欲與共誅亂者。

translations.literal: When Li Siyuan was pressed by the mutineers, Li Shaorong had ten thousand men encamped south of the city. Siyuan sent seven adjutants in succession—including Zhang Qianzhao and Gao Xingzhou—to summon him, wishing to join forces in putting down the mutineers.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Siyuan was held by the mutineers, Li Shaorong had ten thousand men camped south of the city. Siyuan sent seven adjutants in turn—among them Zhang Qianzhao and Gao Xingzhou—to summon him, hoping to join in crushing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 紹榮疑嗣源之詐，留使者，閉壁不應。

translations.literal: Shaorong suspected Siyuan's treachery, detained the envoys, shut his gates, and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shaorong suspected a trap, held the envoys, closed his camp, and would not answer.

sentences.zh: 及嗣源入鄴都，遂引兵去。

translations.literal: When Siyuan entered the Ye capital, he then led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Once Siyuan had entered the Ye capital, Shaorong marched away.

sentences.zh: 嗣源在魏縣，眾不滿百，又無兵仗；

translations.literal: Siyuan was at Wei County with fewer than a hundred men and no arms;
translations.idiomatic: At Wei County Siyuan had fewer than a hundred followers and no weapons;

sentences.zh: 李紹真所將鎮兵五千，聞嗣源得出，相帥歸之，由是嗣兵稍振。

translations.literal: The five thousand garrison troops under Li Shaozhen, hearing that Siyuan had gotten out, led one another back to him, and from this Siyuan's force gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: When the five thousand garrison troops under Li Shaozhen heard that Siyuan had escaped, they rallied to him one after another, and his force slowly recovered.

sentences.zh: 嗣源泣謂諸將曰：「吾明日當歸籓，上章待罪，聽主上所裁。」

translations.literal: Siyuan wept and told the generals, "Tomorrow I shall return to my fief, submit a memorial accepting blame, and await the sovereign's judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan wept and told his officers, "Tomorrow I shall return to my fief, submit a memorial of confession, and leave myself to the sovereign's judgment."

sentences.zh: 李紹真及中門使安重誨曰：「此策非宜。

translations.literal: Li Shaozhen and the Inner Gate Commissioner An Chonghui said, "This plan is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaozhen and An Chonghui, commissioner of the Inner Gate, said, "That course will not serve.

sentences.zh: 公為元帥，不幸為凶人所劫；

translations.literal: You were the supreme commander and were unfortunately seized by violent men;
translations.idiomatic: You were supreme commander and were seized by violent men through no fault of your own;

sentences.zh: 李紹榮不戰而退，歸朝必以公藉口。

translations.literal: Li Shaorong withdrew without fighting; if you return to court, he will surely use you as his excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaorong retreated without a fight. If you return to court, he will surely make you his scapegoat.

sentences.zh: 公若歸籓，則為據地邀君，適足以實讒慝之言耳。

translations.literal: If you return to your fief, you will appear to hold territory and bar the sovereign's way—this would only confirm the words of slanderers.
translations.idiomatic: If you go back to your fief, you will look as though you hold land and defy the throne—and that will only make the slanders seem true.

sentences.zh: 不若星行詣闕，面見天子，庶可自明。」

translations.literal: Better to travel as swiftly as a star to the palace, face the Son of Heaven in person, and perhaps clear yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Better to ride at once to the capital, face the Son of Heaven, and make your innocence plain."

sentences.zh: 嗣源曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Siyuan said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 丁卯，自魏縣南趣相州，遇馬坊使康福，得馬數千匹，始能成軍。

translations.literal: On dingmao he hurried south from Wei County toward Xiangzhou, met the Horse Pasture Commissioner Kang Fu, obtained several thousand horses, and only then could form an army.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he pressed south from Wei County toward Xiangzhou, met Kang Fu, commissioner of the horse pastures, gained several thousand mounts, and at last had enough to make an army.

sentences.zh: 福，蔚州人也。

translations.literal: Fu was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fu was a man of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使符習將本軍攻鄴都，聞李嗣源軍潰，引兵歸。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Pinglu Fu Xi led his own army to attack the Ye capital; hearing that Li Siyuan's force had collapsed, he withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi, military commissioner of Pinglu, marched his own army against the Ye capital, but when he heard that Li Siyuan's force had broken, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 至淄州，監軍使楊希望遣兵逆擊之，習懼，復引兵而西。

translations.literal: When he reached Zizhou, the army supervisor Yang Xiwang sent troops to intercept and strike him. Xi was afraid and again led his army west.
translations.idiomatic: At Zizhou the army supervisor Yang Xiwang sent troops to block him. Xi took fright and marched west again.

sentences.zh: 青州指揮使王公儼攻希望，殺之，因據其城。

translations.literal: The Qingzhou commander Wang Gongyan attacked Xiwang, killed him, and then seized his city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gongyan, commander of Qingzhou, attacked Xiwang, killed him, and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 時近侍為諸道監軍者，皆恃恩與節度使爭權，及鄴都軍變，所在多殺之。

translations.literal: At this time the palace favorites serving as army supervisors in the various circuits all relied on imperial favor to contend with the military commissioners for power; when the Ye capital mutiny broke out, they were killed in many places.
translations.idiomatic: Palace favorites serving as army supervisors in the circuits had long used imperial favor to wrest power from the military commissioners. After the Ye capital mutiny, they were killed in place after place.

sentences.zh: 安義監軍楊繼源謀殺節度使孔勍，勍先誘而殺之。

translations.literal: The Anyi army supervisor Yang Jiyuan plotted to kill Military Commissioner Kong Qiong; Qiong first lured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Anyi the army supervisor Yang Jiyuan plotted to kill Military Commissioner Kong Qiong, but Qiong lured him in first and killed him.

sentences.zh: 武寧監軍以李紹真從李嗣源，謀殺其元從，據城拒之；

translations.literal: The Wuning army supervisor, because Li Shaozhen had followed Li Siyuan, plotted to kill his original followers and hold the city in resistance;
translations.idiomatic: At Wuning the army supervisor, angered that Li Shaozhen had gone over to Li Siyuan, plotted to kill Shaozhen's old companions and hold the city against them;

sentences.zh: 權知留後淳於晏帥諸將先殺之。

translations.literal: the acting governor Chunyu Yan led the generals in killing him first.
translations.idiomatic: Acting governor Chunyu Yan led the generals in killing him first.

sentences.zh: 晏，登州人也。

translations.literal: Yan was a native of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Yan was a man of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以軍食不足，敕河南尹豫借夏秋稅；

translations.literal: On wuchen, because army provisions were insufficient, an edict ordered the Henan prefect Yu to borrow against the summer and autumn taxes;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, with army rations running short, an edict ordered Prefect Yu of Henan to advance against the summer and autumn taxes;

sentences.zh: 民不聊生。

translations.literal: The people could scarcely live.
translations.idiomatic: The people could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 忠武節度使、尚書令齊王張全義聞李嗣源入鄴都，憂懼不食，辛未，卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Zhongwu and Minister of Works Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi, hearing that Li Siyuan had entered the Ye capital, grew anxious and fearful and would not eat; on xinwei he died at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi, military commissioner of Zhongwu, Minister of Works, and Prince of Qi, heard that Li Siyuan had entered the Ye capital, sank into dread, and refused food. On xinwei he died at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 租庸使以倉儲不足，頗朘刻軍糧，軍士流言益甚。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of Tax and Corvée, because the granaries were insufficient, sharply reduced the soldiers' rations, and the soldiers' whispered complaints grew all the worse.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of Tax and Corvée, finding the granaries bare, cut the soldiers' rations sharply, and muttering in the ranks grew louder still.

sentences.zh: 宰相懼，帥百官上表言：「今租庸已竭，內庫有餘，諸軍室家不能相保，儻不賑救，懼有離心。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were afraid and led the hundred officials in a memorial saying, "The tax revenues are now exhausted, yet the inner treasury still has surplus. The households of the armies cannot preserve one another; if we do not grant relief, we fear they will lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were alarmed and led the hundred officials in a memorial: "Tax revenues are spent, yet the inner treasury still holds surplus. Army families cannot keep themselves. Unless we give relief, we fear the troops will turn away.

sentences.zh: 俟過凶年，其財復集。」

translations.literal: Wait until the bad year passes, and the wealth will gather again."
translations.idiomatic: Once the lean year passes, the treasury will fill again."

sentences.zh: 上即欲從之，劉後曰：「吾夫婦君臨萬國，雖藉武功，亦由天命。

translations.literal: The sovereign was about to agree when Empress Liu said, "We two rule the myriad states; though we rely on martial achievement, it is also by Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was ready to agree when Empress Liu said, "We two rule ten thousand states. Our power rests on arms, but our throne rests on Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 命既在天，人如我何！」

translations.literal: Since fate lies with Heaven, what can men do to us!"
translations.idiomatic: If our fate is in Heaven's hands, what can mere men do to us!"

sentences.zh: 宰相又於便殿論之，後屬耳於屏風後，須臾，出妝具及三銀盆、皇幼子三人於外曰：「人言宮中蓄積多，四方貢獻隨以給賜，所餘止此耳，請鬻以贍軍！」

translations.literal: The chief ministers debated the matter again in the informal hall. The empress listened from behind the screen. After a moment she brought out her toilet articles, three silver basins, and three young imperial sons and said, "People say the palace hoards much wealth. Tributes from the four quarters are given away as they arrive; what remains is only this. Please sell it to feed the army!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers debated again in the side hall. The empress listened from behind the screen. Presently she came out with her toilet set, three silver basins, and three young imperial sons and said, "They say the palace is rich. Tribute from every quarter is spent as it arrives. All that remains is this. Sell it, if you will, to feed the army!"

sentences.zh: 宰相惶懼而退。

translations.literal: The chief ministers withdrew in fear and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers withdrew in dread.

sentences.zh: 李紹榮自鄴都退保衛州，奏李嗣源已叛，與賊合。

translations.literal: Li Shaorong withdrew from the Ye capital to hold Weizhou and memorialized that Li Siyuan had already rebelled and joined with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaorong fell back from the Ye capital to Weizhou and reported that Li Siyuan had rebelled and joined the enemy.

sentences.zh: 嗣源遣使上章自理，一日數輩。

translations.literal: Siyuan dispatched envoys submitting memorials in his own defense, several parties in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan sent envoys with memorials pleading his innocence, several times in a single day.

sentences.zh: 嗣源長子從審為金槍指揮使，帝謂從審曰：「吾深知爾父忠厚，爾往諭朕意，勿使自疑。」

translations.literal: Siyuan's eldest son Congshen served as commander of the Golden Spear Guard. The emperor told Congshen, "I know well that your father is loyal and honest. Go and convey my intent—do not let him doubt himself."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan's eldest son Congshen was commander of the Golden Spear Guard. The emperor told him, "I know your father is steadfast and true. Go tell him my mind, and keep him from doubting himself."

sentences.zh: 從審至衛州，紹榮囚，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Congshen reached Weizhou; Shaorong imprisoned him and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Congshen reached Weizhou. Shaorong seized and imprisoned him and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 從審曰：「公等既不亮吾父，吾亦不能至父所，請復還宿衛。」

translations.literal: Congshen said, "Since you gentlemen will not trust my father, I cannot go to my father's side either. I ask to return to palace guard duty."
translations.idiomatic: Congshen said, "Since you will not believe in my father, I cannot go to him. Let me return to palace guard duty instead."

sentences.zh: 乃釋之。

translations.literal: They then released him.
translations.idiomatic: At that they set him free.

sentences.zh: 帝憐從審，賜名繼璟，待之如子。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on Congshen, bestowed on him the name Jijing, and treated him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied Congshen, gave him the name Jijing, and treated him like his own son.

sentences.zh: 是後嗣源所奏，皆為紹榮所遏，不得通，嗣源由是疑懼。

translations.literal: After this, every memorial Siyuan submitted was blocked by Shaorong and could not get through; because of this Siyuan grew suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, every memorial Siyuan sent was intercepted by Shaorong and never reached the emperor. Siyuan grew wary and afraid.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭曰：「夫事成於果決而敗於猶豫，安有上將與叛卒入賊城，而他日得保無恙乎！

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang said, "Matters succeed through resolute decision and fail through hesitation. How can a senior general who enters a rebel city with mutinous soldiers expect to remain unharmed hereafter!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang said, "Success comes from bold action and failure from wavering. How can a commanding general who has entered a rebel city at the head of mutineers ever hope to come through unscathed?

sentences.zh: 大梁，天下之要會也，願假三百騎先往取之；

translations.literal: Daliang is the key junction of the realm. I wish to borrow three hundred cavalry to go first and seize it;
translations.idiomatic: Daliang is the empire's strategic hub. Give me three hundred horsemen and I will go take it first;

sentences.zh: 若幸而得之，公宜引大軍亟進，如此始可自全。」

translations.literal: If by good fortune we take it, Your Lordship should bring the great army forward at once—only thus can you preserve yourself."
translations.idiomatic: If fortune favors us and we take it, you must march the main army at once. Only then can you secure yourself."

sentences.zh: 突騎都指揮使康義誠曰：「主上無道，軍民怨怒，公從眾則生，守節必死。」

translations.literal: Kang Yicheng, commander of the sudden-cavalry guard, said, "The sovereign is without the Way; soldiers and people alike rage in resentment. If Your Lordship follow the multitude, you will live; if you hold to loyal duty, you will surely die."
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng, commander of the vanguard cavalry, said, "The emperor has lost the Way, and soldiers and civilians seethe with anger. Follow the army and you live; cling to loyalty and you die."

sentences.zh: 嗣源乃令安重誨移檄會兵。

translations.literal: Siyuan then ordered An Chonghui to issue a proclamation summoning troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that Siyuan ordered An Chonghui to circulate a call to arms.

sentences.zh: 義誠，代北胡人也。

translations.literal: Yicheng was a barbarian of the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng was a non-Han from north of Dai.

sentences.zh: 時齊州防禦使李紹虔、泰寧節度使李紹欽、貝州刺史李紹英屯瓦橋，北京右廂馬軍都指揮使安審通屯奉化軍，嗣源皆遣使召之。

translations.literal: At the time the Defender of Qizhou Li Shaoqian, the Military Commissioner of Taining Li Shaoqin, and the Prefect of Beizhou Li Shaoying were encamped at Waqiao, and An Shentong, commander of the right wing of the northern capital horse army, was encamped at Fenghua. Siyuan sent envoys to summon them all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaoqian, defender of Qizhou; Li Shaoqin, military commissioner of Taining; and Li Shaoying, prefect of Beizhou were then posted at Waqiao, while An Shentong, commander of the Beijing right-wing cavalry, held Fenghua. Siyuan sent envoys to summon them all.

sentences.zh: 紹英，瑕丘人，本姓房，名知溫；

translations.literal: Shaoying was a native of Xiaqiu; his original surname was Fang and his given name Zhiwen;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoying was from Xiaqiu; born Fang Zhiwen,

sentences.zh: 審通，金全之侄也。

translations.literal: Shentong was a nephew of Jin Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong was Jin Quan's nephew.

sentences.zh: 嗣源家在真定，虞候將王建立先殺其監軍，由是獲全。

translations.literal: Siyuan's family was in Zhending; the adjutant general Wang Jianli first killed their army supervisor, and thereby they were preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan's family was in Zhending. The adjutant general Wang Jianli killed the army supervisor there first, and thus they escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 建立，遼州人也。

translations.literal: Jianli was a native of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli was from Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 李從珂自橫水將所部兵由盂縣趣鎮州，與王建立軍合，倍道從嗣源。

translations.literal: Li Congke led his troops from Hengshui by way of Yuxian toward Zhenzhou, joined Wang Jianli's army, and, marching at double speed, followed Siyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congke marched from Hengshui with his command through Yuxian toward Zhenzhou, linked up with Wang Jianli, and raced to join Siyuan.

sentences.zh: 嗣源以李紹榮在衛州，謀自白皋濟河，分三百騎使石敬瑭將之前驅，李從珂為殿，於是軍勢大盛。

translations.literal: Because Li Shaorong was at Weizhou, Siyuan planned to cross the river from Baigao, detached three hundred cavalry for Shi Jingtang to lead as vanguard, and made Li Congke the rearguard; thus the army's strength greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Shaorong holding Weizhou, Siyuan planned to cross the river at Baigao. He gave Shi Jingtang three hundred horsemen as vanguard and Li Congke the rear guard. His army's strength swelled.

sentences.zh: 嗣源從子從璋自鎮州引軍而南，過邢州，邢人奉為留後。

translations.literal: Siyuan's nephew Congzhang led his army south from Zhenzhou; passing Xingzhou, the people of Xing installed him as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan's nephew Congzhang marched south from Zhenzhou. At Xingzhou the locals hailed him as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔懷遠指揮使白從暉將騎兵扼河陽橋，帝乃出金帛給賜諸軍，樞密宣徽使及供奉內使景進等皆獻金帛以助給賜。

translations.literal: On guiyou, an edict ordered Huaiyuan Commander Bai Conghui to lead cavalry to hold the Heyang Bridge. The emperor then distributed gold and silks to reward the armies; the Military Affairs and Court Ceremonial commissioners and the inner-service envoy Jing Jin and others all contributed gold and silks to assist in the distribution.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor ordered Huaiyuan Commander Bai Conghui to take cavalry and hold Heyang Bridge. He then distributed gold and silk among the armies, and Military Affairs Commissioner and Court Ceremonial Commissioner Jing Jin and others of the inner service contributed gold and silk to help pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 軍士負物而詬曰：「吾妻子已殍死，得此何為！」

translations.literal: Soldiers, burdened with goods, cursed, saying, "Our wives and children have already starved to death—what use is this to us!"
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers loaded with goods cursed aloud: "Our wives and children are already dead of hunger. What good is this to us!"

sentences.zh: 甲戌，李紹榮自衛州至洛陽，帝如鷂店勞之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Li Shaorong came from Weizhou to Luoyang, and the emperor went to Yaodian to welcome and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Li Shaorong arrived in Luoyang from Weizhou, and the emperor went to Yaodian to receive and honor him.

sentences.zh: 紹榮曰：「鄴都亂兵已遣其黨翟建白據博州，欲濟河襲暉、汴，願陛下幸關東招撫之。」

translations.literal: Shaorong said, "The mutinous soldiers of the Ye capital have sent their partisan Zhai Jianbai to seize Bozhou; they mean to cross the river and strike Hui and Bian. I beg Your Majesty to go east of the pass to pacify them."
translations.idiomatic: Shaorong said, "The Ye mutineers have sent their agent Zhai Jianbai to hold Bozhou and plan to cross the river and strike Hui and Bian. I ask that Your Majesty go to the east to win them back."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 景進等言於帝曰：「魏王未至，康延孝初平，西南猶未安；

translations.literal: Jing Jin and the others said to the emperor, "The Prince of Wei has not yet arrived; Kang Yanxiao has only just been pacified, and the southwest is still unsettled;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Jin and others told the emperor, "The Prince of Wei has not returned, Kang Yanxiao has only just been subdued, and the southwest is still unstable;

sentences.zh: 王衍族黨不少，聞車駕東征，恐其為變，不若除之。」

translations.literal: Wang Yan's clansmen and partisans are not few. Hearing that the imperial carriage is campaigning east, I fear they will make trouble—it would be better to eliminate them."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan still has many kinsmen and followers. Hearing that you march east, they may rise up. Better to remove them now."

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣中使向延嗣繼敕往誅之，敕曰：「王衍一行，並從殺戳。」

translations.literal: The emperor then dispatched the palace envoy Xiang Yansi with continuous edicts to execute them. The edict read, "Wang Yan's entire party—all are to be slain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace envoy Xiang Yansi with repeated orders to kill them. The edict ran: "Put to death Wang Yan and all who traveled with him."

sentences.zh: 已印畫，樞密使張居翰覆視，就殿柱揩去「行」字，改為「家」字，由是蜀百官及衍僕役獲免者千餘人。

translations.literal: After it had been sealed and signed, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Juhun reviewed it again; beside a hall pillar he rubbed out the character for "traveling party" and changed it to the character for "household." Thus more than a thousand Shu officials and Yan's servants and retainers were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Once the seal was affixed, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Juhun reviewed the order. At a hall pillar he erased "party" and substituted "household." More than a thousand Shu officials and Yan's household staff were spared.

sentences.zh: 延嗣至長安，盡殺衍宗族於秦川驛。

translations.literal: Yansi reached Chang'an and killed all of Yan's clan at the Qinchuan post station.
translations.idiomatic: When Yansi reached Chang'an he slaughtered Yan's entire clan at Qinchuan Post.

sentences.zh: 衍母徐氏且死，呼曰：「吾兒以一國迎降，不免族誅，信義俱棄，吾知汝行亦受禍矣！」

translations.literal: Yan's mother, Lady Xu, on the point of death, called out, "My son surrendered an entire state and yet could not escape execution of the whole clan—both trust and righteousness were cast aside. I know that your course too will meet with calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan's mother Lady Xu, facing death, cried out, "My son surrendered a whole kingdom and still could not escape clan extermination. Faith and honor were both cast away. Your path too will bring disaster upon you!"

sentences.zh: 乙亥，帝發洛陽；

translations.literal: On yihai, the emperor departed Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor left Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 丁丑，次汜水；

translations.literal: On dingchou, he halted at Sishui;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he encamped at Sishui;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，遣李紹榮將騎兵循河而東。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he dispatched Li Shaorong to lead cavalry eastward along the river.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he sent Li Shaorong east with cavalry along the river.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源親黨從帝者多亡去；

translations.literal: Many of Li Siyuan's kin and partisans who had accompanied the emperor fled away;
translations.idiomatic: Many of Li Siyuan's relatives and allies traveling with the emperor deserted;

sentences.zh: 或勸李繼璟宜早自脫，繼璟終無行意。

translations.literal: Some urged Li Jijing that he should break away early, but Jijing to the end had no thought of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Li Jijing to slip away while he still could, but Jijing refused to consider it.

sentences.zh: 帝屢遣繼璟詣嗣源，繼璟固辭，願死於帝前以明赤誠。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent Jijing to go to Siyuan, but Jijing firmly declined, saying he wished to die before the emperor to make clear his loyal heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly ordered Jijing to go to Siyuan. Jijing steadfastly refused, saying he would rather die before the emperor to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝聞嗣源在黎陽，強遣繼璟渡河召之，道遇李紹榮，紹榮殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Siyuan was at Liyang and forced Jijing to cross the river and summon him. On the road he met Li Shaorong, and Shaorong killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Siyuan was at Liyang, the emperor compelled Jijing to cross the river and summon him. On the way he met Li Shaorong, who killed him.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐有疾，如衣錦軍，命鎮海、鎮東節度使留後傳瓘監國。

translations.literal: The King of Wuyue, Qian Liu, was ill; he went to the Yijin garrison and ordered Fu Zun, acting governor of the Zhenhai and Zhendong circuit, to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu of Wuyue fell ill and went to Yijin Army. He ordered Fu Zun, acting governor of the Zhenhai and Zhendong circuits, to supervise the realm.

sentences.zh: 吳徐溫遣使來問疾，左右勸鏐勿見，鏐曰：「溫陰狡，此名問疾，實使之覘我也。」

translations.literal: Xu Wen of Wu sent envoys to inquire after his illness. Those around Liu urged him not to receive them. Liu said, "Wen is secretly cunning. This is called inquiring after illness; in truth he is sending men to spy on me."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen of Wu sent envoys to ask after his health. Attendants urged Liu not to see them. Liu said, "Wen is sly and deceitful. This is called a sick visit, but in truth he means to spy on me."

sentences.zh: 強出見之。

translations.literal: He forced himself to go out and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged himself out to receive them.

sentences.zh: 溫果聚兵欲襲吳越，聞鏐疾瘳而止。

translations.literal: Wen indeed gathered troops intending to attack Wuyue, but when he heard that Liu's illness had mended, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had indeed massed troops to strike Wuyue, but halted when he heard Liu had recovered.

sentences.zh: 鏐尋還錢塘。

translations.literal: Before long Liu returned to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu returned to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 吳以右僕射、同平章事徐知誥為侍中，右僕射嚴可求兼門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Wu appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Associate Chief Councillor Xu Zhigao as Palace Attendant, and Right Vice Director Yan Keqiu concurrently as Vice Director under the Gate and Associate Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu made Right Vice Director and Associate Chief Councillor Xu Zhigao a Palace Attendant, and Right Vice Director Yan Keqiu also Vice Director under the Gate and Associate Chief Councillor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝發汜水。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the emperor departed from Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor marched from Sishui.

sentences.zh: 辛已，李嗣源至白皋，遇山東上供絹數船，取以賞軍。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Li Siyuan reached Baigao and encountered several boats of silk tribute from Shandong; he took them to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Siyuan reached Baigao, found several tribute boats of Shandong silk, and used them to reward his troops.

sentences.zh: 安重誨從者爭舟，行營馬步使陶□斬以徇，由是軍中肅然。

translations.literal: An Chonghui's followers fought over the boats; Tao □, camp horse-and-foot commissioner, executed one as a warning, and thereafter the army was sternly disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui's men scuffled over the boats. Camp commander Tao [—] executed one as an example, and discipline returned to the ranks.

sentences.zh: □，許州人也。

translations.literal: □ was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [—] was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣源濟河，至滑洲，遣人招符習，習與嗣源會於胙城，安審通亦引兵來會。

translations.literal: Siyuan crossed the river and reached Huazhou; he sent men to summon Fu Xi. Xi joined Siyuan at Zuocheng, and An Shentong also brought his troops to rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan crossed the river to Huazhou and summoned Fu Xi. Xi met him at Zuocheng, and An Shentong joined with his troops as well.

sentences.zh: 知汴州孔循遣使奉表西迎帝，亦遣使北輸密款於嗣源，曰：「先至者得之。」

translations.literal: Kong Xun, prefect of Bianzhou, sent envoys bearing a petition westward to welcome the emperor, and also sent envoys north to offer secret allegiance to Siyuan, saying, "Whoever arrives first will take possession."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun, prefect of Bianzhou, sent envoys west with a petition welcoming the emperor and envoys north with secret pledges to Siyuan, saying, "Whoever gets here first wins."

sentences.zh: 先是，帝遣騎將滿城西方鄴守汴州；

translations.literal: Previously, the emperor had dispatched the cavalry general Man Cheng and Xifang Ye to hold Bianzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent cavalry generals Man Cheng and Xifang Ye to hold Bianzhou;

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭使裨將李瓊以勁兵突入封丘門，敬瑭踵其後，自西門入，遂據其城，西方鄴請降。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang had his subordinate general Li Qiong burst into the city through the Fengqiu Gate with crack troops; Jingtang followed behind, entered through the west gate, and seized the city. Xifang Ye requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang sent Li Qiong with elite troops through Fengqiu Gate; Jingtang followed through the west gate and took the city. Xifang Ye surrendered.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭使人趣嗣源；

translations.literal: Jingtang sent men to urge Siyuan forward;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang sent word urging Siyuan to hurry;

sentences.zh: 壬午，嗣源入大梁。

translations.literal: On renwu, Siyuan entered Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Siyuan entered Daliang.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝至滎澤東，命龍驤指揮使姚彥溫將三千騎為前軍，曰：「汝曹汴人也，吾入汝境，不欲使它軍前驅，恐擾汝室家。」

translations.literal: That day the emperor reached the east of Xingze and ordered Dragon Cavalry Commander Yao Yanwen to lead three thousand horsemen as the vanguard, saying, "You fellows are men of Bian. When I enter your territory I do not wish another army to go ahead as vanguard, lest your households be disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor reached east of Xingze and ordered Dragon Cavalry Commander Yao Yanwen to lead three thousand horsemen as vanguard. He said, "You are men of Bian. I enter your land and do not want other troops going first, for fear your families would be harmed."

sentences.zh: 厚賜而遣之。

translations.literal: He rewarded them generously and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them rich rewards and dispatched them.

sentences.zh: 彥溫即以其眾叛歸嗣源，謂嗣源曰：「京師危迫，主上為元行欽所惑，事勢已離，不可復事矣。」

translations.literal: Yanwen at once led his force in rebellion to join Siyuan and said to Siyuan, "The capital is in peril; the sovereign is deluded by Yuan Xingqin; the situation has already come apart—it is impossible to serve him again."
translations.idiomatic: Yanwen immediately defected with his men to Siyuan and said, "The capital is in dire straits. The emperor is beguiled by Yuan Xingqin. The realm has come apart. We cannot serve him any longer."

sentences.zh: 嗣源曰：「汝自不忠，何言之悖也！」

translations.literal: Siyuan said, "You yourself are disloyal—how perverse your words!"
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan said, "You are the disloyal one. What nonsense you speak!"

sentences.zh: 即奪其兵。

translations.literal: He immediately stripped them of their arms.
translations.idiomatic: At once he seized their command.

sentences.zh: 指揮使潘環守王村寨，有芻粟數萬，帝遣騎視之，環亦奔大梁。

translations.literal: Commander Pan Huan held Wangji village; there were tens of thousands of fodder and grain. The emperor sent cavalry to inspect it, but Huan too fled to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Pan Huan held Wangji Stockade with tens of thousands of grain and fodder. The emperor sent cavalry to check, but Huan also fled to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 帝至萬勝鎮，聞嗣源已據大梁，諸軍離叛，神色沮喪，登高歎曰：「吾不濟矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor reached Wansheng garrison, heard that Siyuan had already seized Daliang, and that the armies were deserting and rebelling. His expression fell; climbing high he sighed and said, "My cause is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: At Wansheng the emperor learned Siyuan held Daliang and his armies were melting away. Despondent, he climbed a height and cried, "I am finished!"

sentences.zh: 即命旋師，是夜復至汜水。

translations.literal: He ordered the army to turn back, and that night returned again to Sishui.
