translations.idiomatic: He turned the army around and that night was back at Sishui.

sentences.zh: 帝之出關也，扈從兵二萬五千，及還，已失萬餘人，乃留秦州都指揮使張唐以步騎三千守關。

translations.literal: When the emperor went out through the pass, the escorting troops numbered twenty-five thousand; by the time he returned he had already lost more than ten thousand. He then left Qinzhou Commander Zhang Tang with three thousand infantry and cavalry to hold the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor left the pass he had twenty-five thousand escorts; on return more than ten thousand were gone. He left Zhang Tang of Qinzhou with three thousand foot and horse to hold the pass.

sentences.zh: 癸未，帝還過罌子谷，道狹，每遇衛士執兵仗者，輒以善言撫之曰：「適報魏王又進西川金銀五十萬，到京當盡給爾曹。」

translations.literal: On guiwei, as the emperor returned through Yingzi Valley, the road was narrow. Whenever he met guards bearing weapons, he would soothe them with kind words, saying, "We have just received word that the Prince of Wei has again delivered five hundred thousand in gold and silver from the western Shu; when it reaches the capital it will all be given to you."
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, returning through Yingzi Valley on a narrow road, the emperor spoke kindly to every armed guard he passed: "Word just came that the Prince of Wei sent five hundred thousand in Shu gold and silver. When it reaches the capital you shall have every bit of it."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下賜已晚矣，人亦不感聖恩！」

translations.literal: They replied, "Your Majesty's grants come too late—men no longer feel the sovereign's grace!"
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Your gifts come too late. No one feels your grace anymore!"

sentences.zh: 帝流涕而已。

translations.literal: The emperor could only weep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could only weep.

sentences.zh: 又索袍帶賜從官，內庫使張容哥稱頒給已盡，衛士叱容哥曰：「致吾君失社稷，皆此閹豎輩也。」

translations.literal: He again asked for robes and belts to reward the attending officials; Inner Treasury Commissioner Zhang Rongge said the grants were already exhausted. The guards shouted at Rongge, "It is eunuchs like these who caused our lord to lose the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again for robes and belts for his attendants. Inner Treasury Commissioner Zhang Rongge said there were none left. Guards cursed Rongge: "Eunuchs like you lost our lord his empire!"

sentences.zh: 抽刀逐之；

translations.literal: They drew swords and chased him;
translations.idiomatic: They drew swords and chased him down;

sentences.zh: 或救之，獲免。

translations.literal: Someone rescued him, and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Others intervened and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 容哥謂同類曰：「皇后吝財致此，今乃歸咎於吾輩；

translations.literal: Rongge said to his fellows, "The empress's stinginess with wealth brought us to this—now blame is heaped on us;
translations.idiomatic: Rongge told his fellows, "The empress's greed brought this on us. Now they blame us;

sentences.zh: 事若不測，吾輩萬段，吾不忍待也！」

translations.literal: if matters go awry, we will be torn limb from limb—I cannot bear to wait for that!"
translations.idiomatic: if things turn worse we'll be hacked to pieces. I won't wait for that!"

sentences.zh: 因赴河死。

translations.literal: He then threw himself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 甲申，帝至石橋西，置酒悲涕，謂李紹榮等諸將曰：「卿輩事吾以來，急難富貴靡不同之；

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor reached the west of Shiqiao, set out wine, and wept in grief. He said to the generals Li Shaorong and the others, "Since you gentlemen have served me, in hardship and in wealth we have shared alike;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor reached west of Shiqiao, poured wine, and wept. He said to Li Shaorong and the other generals, "You have served me through peril and prosperity alike;

sentences.zh: 今致吾至此，皆無一策以相救乎！」

translations.literal: now you have brought me to this pass—is there not a single plan among you to save me!"
translations.idiomatic: and now you leave me here with not one plan to save me!"

sentences.zh: 諸將百餘人，皆截發置地，誓以死報，因相與號泣。

translations.literal: More than a hundred generals all cut off their hair and placed it on the ground, swearing to repay him with their deaths, and together they wailed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred officers cut their hair and laid it before him, swearing to die for him, and all wept together.

sentences.zh: 是日晚，入洛城。

translations.literal: That evening they entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That evening they entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源命石敬瑭將前軍趣汜水收撫散兵，嗣源繼之；

translations.literal: Li Siyuan ordered Shi Jingtang to lead the vanguard toward Sishui to gather and pacify scattered troops; Siyuan followed behind;
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan sent Shi Jingtang ahead toward Sishui to rally stragglers, with Siyuan following;

sentences.zh: 李紹虔、李紹英引兵來會。

translations.literal: Li Shaoqian and Li Shaoying brought their troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaoqian and Li Shaoying joined with their forces.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，宰相、樞密使共奉：「魏王西軍將至，車駕宜且控扼汜水，收撫散兵以俟之。」

translations.literal: On bingxu, the chief ministers and Military Affairs commissioners jointly memorialized, "The Prince of Wei's western army is about to arrive. The imperial carriage should for the present hold Sishui, gather and pacify scattered troops, and wait for it."
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the chief ministers and military commissioners jointly advised, "The Prince of Wei's western army is coming. Your Majesty should hold Sishui, rally the scattered troops, and wait."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，自出上東門閱騎兵，戒以詰旦東行。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, went out himself through the Upper East Gate to review the cavalry, and ordered them to march east at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, went through the Upper East Gate to inspect the cavalry, and ordered them east at dawn.
